odeProperty.value: A technical guide introducing eXeLearning, a free and open source tool for creating digital educational content and Open Educational Resources (OER). The manual is organised into sections covering an introduction to the tool, the workspace, creating and editing content with iDevices, project management, and exporting and publishing materials, providing a complete and organised overview of its educational use.

odeComponent.htmlView:
eXeLearning Manual


 

A practical guide to creating, editing and publishing Open Educational Resources (OER) with eXeLearning, a free and open source tool designed to make educational content creation easier.

Last revised: 29/10/2026

eXe version: 4.0.6

odeComponent.htmlView:
eXeLearning is a free and open source software application (open source) designed for creation and editing of interactive digital resources. It is a tool that makes it easy to incorporate a wide variety of content — text, images, videos, interactive activities and games — in a structured way, with a clear and attractive appearance.

Resources created with eXeLearning have a responsive design, so they display correctly on any device. They can be exported in standard formats such as HTML, SCORM or EPUB3, making them easy to share through platforms and repositories.

Also, eXeLearning promotes the creation of Open Educational Resources (OER), promoting shared knowledge and open education.

The origin of eXeLearning dates back to the early 2000s, as part of the  eXeLearning.org, developed in New Zealand to make it easier to create digital educational content without advanced programming knowledge.

In 2010, the INTEF (then the Institute of Educational Technologies, ITE) took over development of the project and promoted eXeLearning.net as a successor to the original project. Development was coordinated by Cedec, an agency under INTEF and the Government of Extremadura. Since then, eXeLearning has become an established collaborative project involving users, public administrations and various educational organisations.

Over the years, the tool has made significant progress, adding new features and usability improvements while its user community has grown. One of the most significant milestones was undoubtedly the release of Version 3.0 in 2025, which brought a major overhaul of the code and interface, as well as significant improvements such as collaborative working in the online version.


Today, eXeLearning continues to evolve through close collaboration between the Ministry of Education, Vocational Training and Sport and the education authorities of the autonomous communities. It is an active project with an agile development process that enables new versions to be released continuously, bringing improvements to functionality and usability and new possibilities for creating digital educational resources.

odeComponent.htmlView:
eXeLearning is developed through close collaboration between the Spanish Ministry of Education, Vocational Training and Sport (MEFPD), through Cedec-INTEF, and regional education authorities, including those of Extremadura, the Canary Islands, Madrid, the Valencian Community, Galicia and Andalusia.

The project also thrives thanks to the active participation of its community, which contributes ideas, bug reports and suggestions. It also provides support through channels such as Telegram, where people answer questions and openly share knowledge.

eXeLearning development is managed entirely in the open on GitHub, which serves as the central hub for the project. Users and developers can:

  • Report issues or suggest improvements
  • Set up a local environment in minutes using Docker commands, or clone the repository.
  • Read the complete documentation.
  • Fork the project, create branches, make changes and submit Pull Requests.

The community on GitHub is always available to answer questions and receive bug reports in the issues. This open approach strengthens the collaborative nature and continuous improvement of eXeLearning.

odeComponent.htmlView:
Users have several ways to access the tool and create digital educational content. The aim is to make it easy to use in different contexts: from those who need a quick, simple option to those who need to work offline, collaborate in the cloud or integrate eXe into platforms such as Moodle, WordPress or Omeka-S.

The infographic “Quick guide: choose your version of eXeLearning” summarises these options and helps each user choose the most suitable one for their needs.

 



1. Online Version


A major feature of this release is its focus on the online version, available at https://online.exelearning.net.

This option is designed for those who want to start working immediately, without installing anything on their computer. Simply open it in a browser to create, edit and download educational content.

The online version is therefore the quickest and simplest option for teachers. It lets them work with eXeLearning from any computer with an internet connection and then download the materials they create to keep them or publish them wherever needed.

Bear in mind that this version does not work as cloud storage. It lets you create and download content, but does not store projects online permanently. Once you finish working, it is therefore advisable to download the file and keep it on your computer or in your usual storage location.

You can also install your own online eXe instance on your server.

2. Desktop version

The desktop version is intended for those who prefer install eXeLearning on their own computer. It is the appropriate option when you need to work without an internet connection or want to save projects locally.

This option lets teachers install the application on their computer, create educational content and store it directly on their device. It is especially useful in schools with limited connectivity or for teachers who usually work on the same device. 

3. Cloud Version

The Cloud version is intended for users, schools or institutions that need a server installation of eXeLearning. This option lets them work in a cloud environment and offers a more complete experience, combining content creation, editing, project storage and collaboration between users.

This is the most advanced option, particularly suited to organisations that want to centralise their use of eXeLearning. In addition to enabling several users to create and edit content collaboratively, it includes an administration page for managing access credentials, controlling storage space and monitoring projects hosted on the platform.

This administration area also allows user support to be provided and styles and iDevices to be installed for the whole working community. The Cloud version therefore helps both to create content and to organise and maintain a shared environment tailored to the needs of the school or institution.

This option is particularly useful for teaching teams that develop materials together, departments that share resources or institutions that want to provide a shared space for creating, managing and publishing educational content.

4. Plugins and integrations

The fourth way to use eXeLearning is through LMS/CMS plugins, designed for those who want to use eXeLearning directly within platforms such as Moodle, WordPress or Omeka-S.

In this case, eXe is integrated as an editor within the publishing environment itself. This makes it easy to create, edit and publish content without leaving the usual working platform. It is a useful option for schools, teachers or administrators who already use these systems and want to incorporate eXeLearning into their daily workflow.

See the manual "eXeLearning integration solutions"

You can try collaborative editing by visiting https://cloud-demo.exelearning.net/ as a guest.

IMPORTANT NOTICE

Important information about working with the eXe Cloud demo:

  • There are no assigned users or storage space.
  • The projects are not saved automatically. If you want to keep the content you create, you must download the .elpx file before closing.
  • You can share the link with another person and work simultaneously in real time. When anyone closes their browser, they will no longer be able to access the project, because is not stored on the server in this demo mode.

 To use the full functionality of eXeLearning Cloud (including storage, user management and project recovery), you need to install eXe Cloud on a server and manage storage space and user access.

Many education authorities are already working on this so that they can offer it to their teachers soon. If you are interested in this functionality, ask your institution or education authority.

odeComponent.htmlView:
The eXeLearning interface is designed to be intuitive and accessible, making it easy for teachers to create interactive educational materials. It is divided into three main sections:

  • Menu bar: includes key tools for project management.
  • Sidebar: contains the project title, the Structure panel and the iDevices panel.
  • Central area: Content editing area.

odeComponent.htmlView:
This bar at the top contains the essential tools for managing the project: File, Utilities and Help, as well as access to other features.

File Menu

This menu lets us manage our projects. We can open elp/elpx files and editable ZIP or SCORM files created with eXe. We can also open EPUB files created with eXe 3 or later.

It also lets us share, print, export or download them in various standard formats. These include web formats (HTML), e-books (ePub3) and educational standards such as SCORM or IMS, which are needed for working with platforms such as Moodle.

PROJECT PROPERTIES

In this window, which also appears when starting any project, the different tabs allow us to:

  • Metadata: Enter the basic project details (metadata).
  • Export options: Choose export preferences, such as adding a page counter, an accessibility toolbar or a search tool.
  • Grading: Set the minimum score for graded activities.
  • Custom code: Add custom code.
  • Screenshot: Set the image to be used as a preview of the resource on different platforms.

EXE CLOUD OPTIONS

The Cloud version also provides additional options:

  • Project manager. Clicking Open displays a project window where you can:
    • access the history of your saved projects
    • access projects shared with your account
    • open a project stored on your computer
    • clone projects
    • delete projects
  • Share. Allows you to invite other people to edit the project. In 4.0.6, editing access and the public read-only link are managed separately; see Publishing and sharing to share the resource with students.

Utilities menu

From this menu, we can access the following functions:

  • Search: lets us search for words or text within the resource while editing, making it easier to review and update extensive content.
  • Resource report: a table of all the resources (files, images, videos, etc.) used throughout the project, showing the page and box in which each is located. It can be downloaded in CSV format.
  • Link validation: a table of broken links in the project, showing the page and box in which each is located. It can be downloaded in CSV format.
  • File Manager: makes it easier to organise and manage materials centrally. Here we can upload images and documents, insert them into any iDevice, rename or delete them, and organise them into folders.
  • Image Optimizer: lets us reduce the size of selected images in the resource by choosing the desired optimisation level. 
  • Styles: lets us choose from several predefined styles or import one from our computer.
  • Preview: shows how the content will look when exported as a website.

Help menu

Contains information about eXeLearning, the current version, legal notices, the website and other relevant project information.

Shortcuts

At the top right of the interface, we find shortcuts to some of the features already described

  • Redo/Undo: lets us redo or undo actions performed outside iDevices (for example, in the structure or in certain settings). Within iDevices, the text editor’s redo/undo functions remain available.
  • User profile. It gives access to:
    • User preferences. Set the content language and license.
    • Log out / Exit.

odeComponent.htmlView:
This side panel is used both to organise the project and to access the content blocks that will be inserted into its pages.

Title

Project title. The title can also be entered or changed in Project Properties.

Structure Panel

The Structure panel lets us organise the content into pages and subpages.

To access the options for a page, select it and click the three dots. From there, you can add a subpage, clone, export or delete the page, and manage its properties. You can also import content:

  • An iDevice or a box, which will be imported at the end of the selected page.
  • A page or an entire project, which will be inserted as subpages of the selected page.

The options to delete, clone, import and insert a new page also appear as shortcuts at the top of the panel.

In the page properties, we can change its title, hide it from the work area or display a different title from the one in the navigation menu. We can also highlight the page or exclude it from the export.

iDevices Panel

iDevices (content blocks) are the central element of the tool. They are blocks or “puzzle pieces” that make it easy to add different types of content, including text, images, videos, audio and interactive activities. In the interface, iDevices are grouped into categories to make them easy to find:

  • Information and Presentation. Display information, organise resources or enrich content with accessibility features and different media.
  • Assessment and Tracking. Provide quizzes and other tools to check knowledge or progress, with the option to give feedback.
  • Games. Use game mechanics to motivate and reinforce learning without assessment pressure.
  • Interactive Activities. Require direct interaction, encouraging active learning through trial and error.
  • Science. Designed for content in specific subjects or topic areas.

Clicking each section displays the iDevices in that category. Each iDevice will be covered in detail later.

odeComponent.htmlView:
This is the main work area where the project’s content is built. To start creating, click or drag the chosen iDevice from the iDevices panel or the favourites bar at the bottom of the work area. The iDevices on this bar can be changed by clicking the cog on the right.


HOW CONTENT IS ORGANIZED: BOXES AND IDEVICES

The content of each page is organised into boxes. Each box can have an icon and a title, and can contain as many iDevices as we want.

When we drag an iDevice into the work area, we can place it inside an existing box (above or below other iDevices) or directly on the canvas. In the latter case, a box is created automatically to contain it. Once the iDevice has been edited and saved, we can edit the box’s title and icon.

Both boxes and iDevices can be cloned, moved, exported and deleted from the toolbar at the top right of each one. The properties also allow us to configure other aspects, such as:

  • whether it is visible in the export
  • whether it is visible only in teacher mode
  • whether it is minimized by default (boxes only)

odeComponent.htmlView:
Next, we will explore two essential elements for creating resources with eXeLearning:

  • iDevices, which let you add and structure interactive content
  • The text editor, an essential tool for shaping and formatting the information presented, is included in many iDevices.

Text Editor

First, we will examine the features included in the Text Editor, an essential tool available in many iDevices that lets us enter and format text, include multimedia elements, structure text, add mathematical or musical notation, or record audio. It is therefore an essential tool used throughout resource creation. We will examine this editor in detail, showing its fundamental importance.

iDevices

The main element for adding content to resources created with eXeLearning is the “iDevice”, or content block. These iDevices enrich resources and bring them to life by allowing a wide variety of materials to be added, from text, images and videos to digital objects, interactive activities and games. iDevices are organised into categories to make content design easier:

  • Information and presentation: Display and structure content, with accessibility features and a range of media.
  • Assessment and tracking: Tools to check knowledge and progress, with the option to provide feedback.
  • Games: Resources that use game mechanics to motivate and reinforce learning without assessment pressure.
  • Interactive activities: Exercises that require direct interaction for active learning.
  • Science: Designed specifically for content in particular subjects or areas

Next, we will explore two essential elements for creating resources with eXeLearning:

  • iDevices, which let you add and structure interactive content
  • The text editor, an essential tool for shaping and formatting the information presented, is included in many iDevices.

Text Editor

First, we will examine the features included in the Text Editor, an essential tool available in many iDevices that lets us enter and format text, include multimedia elements, structure text, add mathematical or musical notation, or record audio. It is therefore an essential tool used throughout resource creation. We will examine this editor in detail, showing its fundamental importance.

iDevices

The main element for adding content to resources created with eXeLearning is the “iDevice”, or content block. These iDevices enrich resources and bring them to life by allowing a wide variety of materials to be added, from text, images and videos to digital objects, interactive activities and games. iDevices are organised into categories to make content design easier:

  • Information and presentation: Display and structure content, with accessibility features and a range of media.
  • Assessment and tracking: Tools to check knowledge and progress, with the option to provide feedback.
  • Games: Resources that use game mechanics to motivate and reinforce learning without assessment pressure.
  • Interactive activities: Exercises that require direct interaction for active learning.
  • Science: Designed specifically for content in particular subjects or areas

The text editor of eXeLearning is TinyMCE, a WYSIWYG editor (what you see is what you get) for HTML. This open source editor is the main interface for entering and editing text in most iDevices.

It offers a main menu with additional features (Edit, Insert, Format, Table, Utilities) and three rows of tools with various options that can be explored in the following image by hovering over its active areas.

Shows the simplified or expanded toolbar

A first row of tools for basic text editing, such as bold, italics, formatting, font size and type, and text or background colour. It works similarly to any word processor, making it easy to add different materials.

The text editor has a second row which includes tools for formatting paragraphs (alignment, line breaks, bulleted and numbered lists, and definition lists) and for inserting or removing hyperlinks, indentation and quotations.

The third row extends its capabilities by allowing the inclusion of text from other sources, code (HTML, mathematical markup in LaTeX and syntax highlighting), dynamic effects (accordion, tabs and carousel) and multimedia elements such as images, videos, audio (recorded directly) and musical notation. Its ability to manage pasted content is essential: it offers options to paste plain text and avoid unwanted code, which is important for keeping HTML clean and making accessible content easier to create

This icon switches the editing area to full screen and back to the smaller view.

Next, we will examine the features that are most significant or differ from those in a typical text editor.

Your browser does not support this tool.

In general, when your browser’s spellchecker detects a spelling error and underlines a word in red in the editor, you can view correction suggestions by holding down the Ctrl and right-clicking on the highlighted word.

In the desktop version on Windows and Linux, you can set one or more spellchecking languages. To do this, open User profile → User preferences → Spell checker languages. Select one or more available languages to check multilingual text, independently of the interface language. Choose System default, or leave all languages unselected, to use the operating system’s language. This option cannot be combined with manually selected languages. Save your preferences to retain the selection.

On macOS, spellchecking languages are managed through the operating system settings.

odeComponent.htmlView:
In eXeLearning, we can copy and paste any text using Ctrl+C, Ctrl+X and Ctrl+V. However, pasting content from an external source can bring unwanted code from the original document, which may cause problems when changing the formatting later.

To avoid this, “Paste as text” is enabled by default. Once the text has been pasted from the clipboard, we can apply the desired formatting or add links directly in the text editor.

If we occasionally need to paste with formatting, we can disable this option by clicking its icon. In this case, we recommend cleaning the code by selecting the text and clicking Main menu > Format > Clear formatting.

Remember that “Paste as text” pastes text without its original formatting, links or styles, BUT ensures that its HTML is clean. This prevents problems when you want to format it or apply a style.

odeComponent.htmlView:
“Definition list” lets us create a list of terms or concepts with hidden definitions or explanations. Clicking a term displays its definition or explanation.

OER

Open Educational Resources (OER) are learning, teaching and research materials in any format and medium that are in the public domain or are copyrighted and have been released under an open licence, allowing others to access them free of charge, reuse, repurpose, adapt and redistribute them.


An open licence respects the intellectual property rights of the copyright holder and grants the public permission to access, reuse, repurpose, adapt and redistribute educational materials.

Free Software

Free software (sometimes called libre software because the English word “free” can be confused with “free of charge”) is software that respects the freedom of all users who acquire it. Once obtained, it can therefore be freely used, copied, studied, modified and redistributed in various ways.

According to its leading advocate, the Free Software Foundation, free software concerns users’ freedom to run, copy, distribute and study software, and even modify it and distribute modified versions. (from Wikipedia)

Procomún

The platform Procomún began in April 2014 with the aim of becoming a meeting place for teachers to exchange views and proposals about educational experiences and learning. At the same time, it served as a reference point for accessing the repository of digital Open Educational Resources (OER) of the Ministry of Education, Vocational Training and Sport and the autonomous communities.

A tooltip lets us include comments throughout the text and define their appearance and behaviour.

"A tooltip (also called a pop-up description) is a visual help, which appears when the cursor is placed over a graphical element, providing additional help to explain that element’s purpose to the user.”. Wikipedia

Avoid overusing tooltips. Do not make them too long or include very wide images. Bear in mind that tooltips only support widths below 300 px. 

A graphical user interface (GUI) is a computer program that acts as a user interface, using a set of images and graphical objects to represent the information and actions available. Its main purpose is to provide a simple visual environment for communicating with a machine’s or computer’s operating system.

odeComponent.htmlView:
The FX button lets us create various effects to structure our content and reduce the need to scroll down.

Accordion

The “Accordion” effect arranges content in a list whose sections can be expanded and collapsed by clicking each heading.

Spring

From 21 March to 20 June, spring marks the start of milder weather after winter. During these months, temperatures gradually rise, days become longer and vegetation begins to grow rapidly. Pollen levels increase during this period, affecting both agriculture and the health of people with allergies.

Summer

Between 21 June and 22 September, summer is the hottest season of the year in the northern hemisphere. Days are longer than nights, increasing exposure to the sun. It is a season associated with rest, holidays and outdoor activities, although it also brings risks such as drought and heatwaves in some regions.

Autumn

From 23 September to 20 December, autumn brings a gradual fall in temperatures and fewer hours of daylight. Deciduous trees commonly lose their leaves, creating characteristic landscapes in shades of brown and ochre. In many countries, this season also marks the start of harvesting and preparations for winter.

Winter

From 21 December to 20 March, winter is the coldest season of the year, with short days and long nights. Much of the northern hemisphere experiences frost and snow, affecting transport, agriculture and everyday life. Heating use increases during this period, which is also associated with major celebrations such as Christmas and New Year.

Tabs

The “Tabs” effect lets us quickly change what is displayed without changing pages.

odeComponent.htmlView:
Creating an accordion effect is very simple. Follow these steps:

1. We click on the buttonfrom the editor.

2. In the window that appears, select the desired effect (Accordion, Tabs, Pagination or Carousel).

3. Editing works similarly whichever effect you choose. A box is created with two headings (which you can change to the titles you want) and two areas for content that can be shown or collapsed. You can edit it and add any type of multimedia resource.

4. To create a new list item, enter its title and content inside the FX box. Select the title and choose the “Heading 2” format.

5. To change the effect, simply click the FX button again and select another one.

odeComponent.htmlView:
When clicking on the icon  a window opens with three tabs:

  • General: lets us insert an image using a URL or an image file.
    • For accessibility, it is advisable to fill in the “Alternative description” and “Image title” fields.
    • To keep the resource’s file size down, it is advisable to optimise images before inserting them or use the “Optimise image” option. This lets us set the file size and quality of the image included in the project, reducing the overall project size.
  • Advanced: alignment and styles.
  • Title and attribution: lets you specify the image author, source and license.

Clicking the Insert/Edit Media icon  opens a window with four tabs:

  • General: lets us insert a multimedia element using a URL or a file, specifying its type, dimensions and other playback options if necessary.
  • Title and attribution: lets you specify the video author, source and license.
  • Attributes: lets you modify the format using code.
  • Subtitles: lets us add a subtitle file (.srt or .vtt) to a video uploaded from the local computer.

If what we have is a embed code, we can use the option :

This option is simpler, but to add a title, attribution or other attributes, we need to use the Insert/Edit Media icon.

odeComponent.htmlView:
A few months ago, what some consider “the greatest scientific discovery in history” was announced: proof of the existence of the Higgs boson. But what exactly is the boson? Why is this discovery so important?

Using this presentation as a starting point, we invite you to carry out your own research into this topic through a series of activities.

Information search:

Find two or three websites with information about the Higgs boson: who discovered it, what theory was proposed, and where and how that theory was finally demonstrated.

It is very important to make sure the information sources you find are suitable and will remain accessible for some time; in other words, that they are stable websites.

Oral presentation:

Using the information obtained from the sources you consulted, prepare an oral presentation explaining the key aspects of the topic we are studying. You can also present the information sources you used.

The presentation must last no more than five minutes. You must use a supporting resource. This can be a presentation you have created or online material similar to the example we showed you.

odeComponent.htmlView:
Support for the main content

7 reasons to use Free Software in schools (based on a text by Richard Stallman)

  • Promotes cooperation. Freedom to share tools and developments between schools and teachers.
  • Encourages autonomy. Freedom to manage the computers used by schools, teachers and students.
  • Saves costs. Freedom to copy and distribute software.
  • Encourages learning. Freedom to read and understand programs’ source code.
  • Develops creativity and imagination. Freedom to create and continuously distribute programs and developments.
  • Prepares learners for digital society. Freedom to choose and design tools, software and equipment.
  • Educates independent, community-minded citizens. Freedom to share technological knowledge.

Audio

Visual support

Several blocks and buttons

Here are the steps for creating a teaching sequence with eXeLearning:

1. Install eXeLearning

It is a free, open source tool, available at https://exelearning.net for operating systems.

2. Create the structure

eXe allows you to create a navigable menu for organize content into pages. This menu has a hierarchical structure that we can organise to suit our needs, with as many nodes and subnodes as required. The menu is available when exporting as a website or publishing the content in an LMS such as Moodle.

3. Add Content

We can insert all kinds of materials using content blocks, or “iDevices”. The text editor lets us include and format text, add images, upload video or audio, and embed content created with other tools. Finally, we can choose one of the available styles or create a custom one. As for organization of content, we recommend:

  • Starting with a motivating activity, a reflection task or an activity that activates prior knowledge, to prepare learners for the tasks that follow.
  • Present tasks to be completed, with clear explanations and, where appropriate, links to documents or websites for finding or consulting information, ICT tools needed to complete the tasks (with a link to a manual or tutorial) and, crucially, the assessment tool for the task, which will also serve as a guide for learners.
  • Add reflection activities throughout the learning process, to develop metacognition, consolidate learning and strengthen the ability to learn how to learn.

4. Add interactivity

We can enrich our sequence with interactive activities that students can use for self-assessment. Some of these activities record results in Moodle, so they can be used for grading. Other iDevices, such as Rubric, can also be included.

5. Save and publish

Once the sequence is complete, we can save it in different formatsdepending on what we want to do with that material:

  • Save the resource locally, on a USB drive or in external storage, and send it to students for reference.
  • Publish it on Procomún and give learners a direct link.
  • Upload it to an LMS such as Moodle.
  • Publish it in other web spaces provided by educational or other institutions 

Do you have any questions?

For questions or suggestions about the tool, we can consult the eXe manual or the Telegram group.

Selecting “UDL Content” from the iDevices list displays the following in eXeLearning:

As with the Text iDevice, we can optionally add:

  • A title.
  • An icon chosen from those available in the selected style (remember that the UDL style offers the most icons for this context, including specific icons with colours associated with the type of UDL content we want to add).
  • A feedback section that expands when the button is clicked (the button text can also be changed).

There are many more options for adding content to this iDevice:

  • First, choose the type of content to insert according to the UDL classification: Engagement, Comprehension or Expression. In some styles (such as UDL), the types of content are distinguished by their associated colour.
  • We can add as many content blocks as we want. Only one appears by default, but we can add more by clicking the icon .
  • Each content block provides several options:
    • Decide whether the content should appear directly (in which case, leave the “Button text” field empty) or when a button is clicked. In the latter case, enter the button text and, if desired, associate the button with one of the available characters.
    • The content box has four tabs where we can provide the same content in different formats to make it easier for all users to understand:
      • Main content, where we add our content (required).
      • Easy read
      • Audio
      • Visual support

Download .elp file

Clicking the “Download source file” iDevice creates a table using the information entered in the metadata.

As well as editing the automatically created table, we can customise the download button by changing its text and colour, and the font size and colour.

In 4.0.6, the default button identifies the format .elpx. Existing iDevices keep the text saved by their author: if your button still says .elp, edit it to say .elpx. Downloads also work on sites such as Omeka S, where the process could previously get stuck at 100%.

odeComponent.htmlView:
DigCompEdu summary

Selected Indicators: 94

1. Professional engagement2. Digital resources3. Teaching and learning4. Assessment and feedback5. Empowering learners6. Facilitating learners’ digital competence
1.11.21.31.41.52.12.22.33.13.23.33.44.14.24.35.15.25.36.16.26.36.46.5
C2C2C2C2C2C2
Area: Professional engagement
  • A1 for competence 1.1. Organisational communication because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Communicates using basic digital etiquette through digital technologies: email, forums, chat, videoconferencing systems, etc.; indicator 2. Uses each tool correctly, adapting it to the communication context; and indicator 3. Knows the features, functions, accessibility options and limitations of communication tools, as well as the regulations governing their use in education.
  • A2 for competence 1.1. Organisational communication because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Knows and applies, under supervision, the acceptable-use policies for organisational communication tools established by the education authority or school owners; and indicator 2. With advice from other teachers and while ensuring accessibility, uses the digital technologies established by the education authority or school owners in a real educational communication context.
  • B1 for competence 1.1. Organisational communication because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Communicates independently and conventionally with members of the educational community, using the most appropriate digital tool from those established for that purpose by the education authority or school owners; and indicator 2. Applies the acceptable-use policies for organisational communication tools established by the education authority or school owners.
  • B2 for competence 1.1. Organisational communication because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Identifies and implements complementary uses of organisational communication tools while respecting the school’s acceptable-use policies; indicator 2. Collaborates in developing or improving the school’s communication plan; and indicator 3. Provides informal support to other teachers in the correct use of technologies for school communication.
  • C1 for competence 1.1. Organisational communication because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Evaluates the functions, performance, accessibility and limitations of the organisational communication tools used by the school to make their use more efficient; indicator 2. Coordinates the development of the school’s digital communication plan, ensuring that it complies with current regulations and includes acceptable-use policy, digital etiquette and workflow considerations; and indicator 3. Trains other members of the school community in the use of digital communication technologies through formally organised activities.
  • C2 for competence 1.1. Organisational communication because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Participates in research projects and the design of organisational communication tools adapted to schools; and indicator 2. Publishes or provides training on new organisational communication strategies in schools.
Area: Digital resources
  • A1 for competence 2.1. Searching for and selecting digital content because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Knows the teaching, technical (licences, accessibility, suitability for students’ ages and achieving objectives) and scientific criteria (source reliability, rigour, etc.) for selecting quality content; indicator 2. Uses search engines that support neutral results, applies efficient search strategies and knows the role of metadata in retrieving content; and indicator 3. Uses a system for organising resources (applications, browser extensions, etc.).
  • A2 for competence 2.1. Searching for and selecting digital content because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. With guidance, identifies the requirements digital content must meet to suit a specific learning situation and applies the corresponding search and selection criteria, including compatibility with the virtual platforms established by the education authority or school owners; and indicator 2. Understands and uses institutional content repositories and those used by the school.
  • B1 for competence 2.1. Searching for and selecting digital content because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Independently applies teaching, technical and scientific criteria when searching for and selecting digital educational content suited to a specific learning situation (for example, reinforcement, extension or deeper exploration); indicator 2. Uses searches to find different content formats (audio, video, images, web, etc.), selecting those that encourage all students’ motivation, engagement and participation in the same activity; and indicator 3. Systematically uses a system for organising and cataloguing selected digital educational content for personal use or within the teaching team.
  • B2 for competence 2.1. Searching for and selecting digital content because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Uses a tool for evaluating and relationally cataloguing digital educational content and takes it into account in search strategies; indicator 2. Informally advises colleagues at the school on using internet search strategies; and indicator 3. Takes a proactive approach to finding new digital content repositories.
  • C1 for competence 2.1. Searching for and selecting digital content because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Coordinates the definition of technological and pedagogical criteria for selecting digital content from a whole-school perspective, using quality standards as a reference; indicator 2. Evaluates search strategies by analysing the quality of the results obtained; and indicator 3. Researches and evaluates new trends in organising internet content to adapt to its evolution (semantic web, big data, faceted searches).
  • C2 for competence 2.1. Searching for and selecting digital content because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Researches how search engines work, their algorithms and the use of metadata to retrieve information, and applies this knowledge to designing new search and cataloguing strategies; and indicator 2. Evaluates quality models for assessing digital educational content and proposes new models or improvements to existing ones to better suit educational practice.
Area: Teaching and learning
  • A1 for competence 3.1. Teaching because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Knows different pedagogical models and approaches to integrating digital technologies that are consistent with those models for teaching; indicator 2. Selectively integrates digital resources into lesson planning according to their suitability for the objectives, content, students, etc.; and indicator 3. Knows the basic features of different digital educational resources and their possible uses in teaching, and uses them in simulated face-to-face or online situations.
  • A2 for competence 3.1. Teaching because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. With help from other teachers, selectively integrates the school’s digital resources into lesson planning according to their suitability for the objectives, learning, students, etc., following the pedagogical model in the school’s educational project; and indicator 2. Implements lesson plans in teaching practice, resolving with help any problems that arise when using digital technologies.
  • B1 for competence 3.1. Teaching because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Selectively integrates the school’s available digital resources into lesson planning, following the pedagogical model in the educational project; indicator 2. Uses the school’s digital resources conventionally and independently, selecting them according to their features, the educational context and the teaching mode (face-to-face, online, distance, hybrid or blended); indicator 3. While using familiar digital resources, assesses their suitability for helping students achieve learning objectives; and indicator 4. Resolves the most common problems arising when integrating digital technologies into teaching and handles unexpected situations with alternative solutions.
  • B2 for competence 3.1. Teaching because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Transfers innovative practices in the educational use of digital technologies to their teaching context, making the necessary adaptations, and adapts previously used digital resources to new learning situations; indicator 2. Integrates digital technologies into planning and teaching so that students must use them in varied, diverse, selective and responsible ways to complete the proposed activities and achieve learning objectives; indicator 3. Resolves technical and pedagogical problems arising in teaching through well-established theoretical and practical knowledge of both general technologies and those specific to the subject or area taught; and indicator 4. Provides informal support to other teachers in implementing digital technologies in the classroom or planning their integration into teaching.
  • C1 for competence 3.1. Teaching because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Researches new strategies for integrating digital resources into planning and teaching, both in the classroom and across the school; indicator 2. Coordinates or leads the design of strategies for integrating digital technologies in the school and aligning them with the educational project and digital plan or strategy, including pedagogical, teaching and technical aspects; indicator 3. Coordinates or collaborates in configuring and administering the school’s digital technologies; and indicator 4. Coordinates school-based training activities to analyse the inclusion of digital technologies in the pedagogical models established in the educational project.
  • C2 for competence 3.1. Teaching because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Creates new models for integrating digital resources into teaching, developing new educational experiences that significantly improve learning; and indicator 2. Coordinates or develops research projects on the impact of digital technology use on learning.
Area: Assessment and feedback
  • A1 for competence 4.1. Assessment strategies because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Knows and configures the most common digital tools according to the different functions of teaching and learning assessment (diagnostic, formative and summative); indicator 2. Designs assessment activities that students complete using digital media; and indicator 3. Knows personal data protection regulations and how they affect information-gathering processes using digital technologies.
  • A2 for competence 4.1. Assessment strategies because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. With guidance, applies the digital assessment technologies provided by the education authority or school owners to collect information on the indicators established in lesson planning; indicator 2. Under supervision, uses the school’s digital technologies to design a varied range of assessment methods (students’ attitudes, work and performance) that allow learning to be monitored appropriately and possible student needs to be identified; indicator 3. With help from other teachers, designs and uses a tool to evaluate their teaching practice using the school’s digital technologies; and indicator 4. Knows and applies, under supervision, the school’s data protection protocol in assessment procedures involving digital technologies.
  • B1 for competence 4.1. Assessment strategies because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Independently uses the digital assessment platforms provided by the education authority or school owners; indicator 2. Diversifies the techniques, methods and tools for assessing students’ learning and their own teaching practice by independently using the school’s digital technologies; and indicator 3. Independently applies the school’s security and personal data protection protocols in assessment processes.
  • B2 for competence 4.1. Assessment strategies because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Combines techniques, methods and tools for collecting digital data on assessment indicators so that the results can be cross-checked through triangulation; and indicator 2. Applies the school’s digital technologies to designing methods and tools that facilitate the assessment of teaching and learning processes involving new teaching strategies.
  • C1 for competence 4.1. Assessment strategies because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Participates in monitoring and evaluating the protocols and digital technologies used by the school to assess teaching and learning, contributing to their revision or the implementation of new strategies; indicator 2. Advises or trains colleagues in using the school’s digital technologies for educational assessment; and indicator 3. Coordinates the integration of digital technologies into the evaluation of the school’s programmes and projects.
  • C2 for competence 4.1. Assessment strategies because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Researches and critically analyses the functions of digital technologies, including emerging ones, that facilitate data collection to assess teaching and learning processes or different aspects of the education system; and indicator 2. Makes innovative proposals for integrating digital technologies, including emerging ones, into educational assessment, respecting the digital rights and safeguards of everyone involved and aligning with the ethical and pedagogical principles in current education laws.
Area: Empowering learners
  • A1 for competence 5.1. Accessibility and inclusion because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Understands how technological resources available in education support universal accessibility and how to integrate them into teaching practice; indicator 2. Understands the positive and negative effects of including digital technologies in teaching and learning; and indicator 3. Knows the principles of universal accessibility and the educational application of digital technologies to include all students, as well as the relevant current regulations.
  • A2 for competence 5.1. Accessibility and inclusion because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Selects and uses basic accessibility options in the school’s technology in controlled environments or with guidance; and indicator 2. Knows the protocols and measures adopted by the school and/or education authority to reduce the digital divide and applies them with guidance from other teachers.
  • B1 for competence 5.1. Accessibility and inclusion because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Independently uses the accessibility options of the school’s technology, selecting those most appropriate for their students; and indicator 2. Collaborates in implementing measures adopted by the education authority and the school to address the digital divide and promote the educational inclusion of all students in the use of digital technologies.
  • B2 for competence 5.1. Accessibility and inclusion because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Evaluates the accessibility options of the school’s available digital technologies to use them selectively and adapt them to the teaching and learning context; and indicator 2. Adapts technological solutions for inclusion in any educational context and teaching and learning situation, enabling all students to participate and progress in the same teaching process.
  • C1 for competence 5.1. Accessibility and inclusion because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Analyses and evaluates the school’s digital technologies as tools for promoting student accessibility and inclusion, proposing improvements so all students can participate in the same teaching process; indicator 2. Actively collaborates in or coordinates the development and evaluation of pedagogical strategies that enable all students to participate together in teaching and learning using digital technologies; and indicator 3. Provides formal advice or training to other teachers on using digital technologies to facilitate accessibility and inclusion for all students in teaching and learning.
  • C2 for competence 5.1. Accessibility and inclusion because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Researches how accessibility and inclusion aspects of digital technologies improve teaching and learning processes, and proposes new pedagogical strategies; and indicator 2. Collaborates in developing new digital technology functions to improve accessibility and educational inclusion.
Area: Facilitating learners’ digital competence
  • A1 for competence 6.1. Media, information and data literacy because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Knows and understands how browsers, search engines, online services and IoT (Internet of Things) devices operate when searching for, processing and retrieving information and data; and indicator 2. Knows the teaching criteria required to help students become competent in searching for, selecting, evaluating and processing relevant, appropriate and reliable information and data, and how this competence is integrated into the curriculum or programme of study.
  • A2 for competence 6.1. Media, information and data literacy because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. With help from other teachers, applies teaching proposals that integrate the content, activities and approaches needed to develop students’ media, information and data literacy, adapting them to the curriculum, educational project and school digital plan; and indicator 2. Applies technical knowledge of content management and the configuration of information search and processing tools to the use of digital technologies provided by the education authority or school owners.
  • B1 for competence 6.1. Media, information and data literacy because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Integrates learning situations into teaching in which students must develop different strategies for searching for, evaluating, selecting and organising information and data; and indicator 2. Selects the most suitable technologies from those provided by the education authority or school owners to develop students’ competence in handling information and data.
  • B2 for competence 6.1. Media, information and data literacy because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Reflects on and evaluates their own practice to design or adapt new pedagogical proposals that help students develop the ability to determine what information they need, how to search for it, select it critically and organise it; and indicator 2. Configures and uses the digital technologies provided by the education authority or school owners in varied and flexible ways so students develop their competence in handling information and data.
  • C1 for competence 6.1. Media, information and data literacy because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Coordinates or contributes to designing and implementing the pedagogical proposals in the school’s digital plan to develop students’ digital competence in media, information and data literacy, and to evaluating their impact on this learning; indicator 2. Evaluates the digital technologies and services used by the school to develop students’ media, information and data literacy in order to propose improvements; and indicator 3. Advises or trains other teachers on pedagogical strategies and the configuration and use of technologies to strengthen students’ digital competence in media, information and data literacy.
  • C2 for competence 6.1. Media, information and data literacy because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Researches the impact of the teaching and pedagogical strategies, technologies and digital services commonly used to develop students’ media, information and data literacy; and indicator 2. Uses research to design new pedagogical proposals to improve the acquisition and development of students’ digital competence in media, information and data literacy.

Area: Professional engagement
  • A1 for competence 1.1. Organisational communication because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Communicates using basic digital etiquette through digital technologies: email, forums, chat, videoconferencing systems, etc.; indicator 2. Uses each tool correctly, adapting it to the communication context; and indicator 3. Knows the features, functions, accessibility options and limitations of communication tools, as well as the regulations governing their use in education.
  • A2 for competence 1.1. Organisational communication because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Knows and applies, under supervision, the acceptable-use policies for organisational communication tools established by the education authority or school owners; and indicator 2. With advice from other teachers and while ensuring accessibility, uses the digital technologies established by the education authority or school owners in a real educational communication context.
  • B1 for competence 1.1. Organisational communication because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Communicates independently and conventionally with members of the educational community, using the most appropriate digital tool from those established for that purpose by the education authority or school owners; and indicator 2. Applies the acceptable-use policies for organisational communication tools established by the education authority or school owners.
  • B2 for competence 1.1. Organisational communication because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Identifies and implements complementary uses of organisational communication tools while respecting the school’s acceptable-use policies; indicator 2. Collaborates in developing or improving the school’s communication plan; and indicator 3. Provides informal support to other teachers in the correct use of technologies for school communication.
  • C1 for competence 1.1. Organisational communication because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Evaluates the functions, performance, accessibility and limitations of the organisational communication tools used by the school to make their use more efficient; indicator 2. Coordinates the development of the school’s digital communication plan, ensuring that it complies with current regulations and includes acceptable-use policy, digital etiquette and workflow considerations; and indicator 3. Trains other members of the school community in the use of digital communication technologies through formally organised activities.
  • C2 for competence 1.1. Organisational communication because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Participates in research projects and the design of organisational communication tools adapted to schools; and indicator 2. Publishes or provides training on new organisational communication strategies in schools.
Area: Digital resources
  • A1 for competence 2.1. Searching for and selecting digital content because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Knows the teaching, technical (licences, accessibility, suitability for students’ ages and achieving objectives) and scientific criteria (source reliability, rigour, etc.) for selecting quality content; indicator 2. Uses search engines that support neutral results, applies efficient search strategies and knows the role of metadata in retrieving content; and indicator 3. Uses a system for organising resources (applications, browser extensions, etc.).
  • A2 for competence 2.1. Searching for and selecting digital content because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. With guidance, identifies the requirements digital content must meet to suit a specific learning situation and applies the corresponding search and selection criteria, including compatibility with the virtual platforms established by the education authority or school owners; and indicator 2. Understands and uses institutional content repositories and those used by the school.
  • B1 for competence 2.1. Searching for and selecting digital content because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Independently applies teaching, technical and scientific criteria when searching for and selecting digital educational content suited to a specific learning situation (for example, reinforcement, extension or deeper exploration); indicator 2. Uses searches to find different content formats (audio, video, images, web, etc.), selecting those that encourage all students’ motivation, engagement and participation in the same activity; and indicator 3. Systematically uses a system for organising and cataloguing selected digital educational content for personal use or within the teaching team.
  • B2 for competence 2.1. Searching for and selecting digital content because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Uses a tool for evaluating and relationally cataloguing digital educational content and takes it into account in search strategies; indicator 2. Informally advises colleagues at the school on using internet search strategies; and indicator 3. Takes a proactive approach to finding new digital content repositories.
  • C1 for competence 2.1. Searching for and selecting digital content because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Coordinates the definition of technological and pedagogical criteria for selecting digital content from a whole-school perspective, using quality standards as a reference; indicator 2. Evaluates search strategies by analysing the quality of the results obtained; and indicator 3. Researches and evaluates new trends in organising internet content to adapt to its evolution (semantic web, big data, faceted searches).
  • C2 for competence 2.1. Searching for and selecting digital content because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Researches how search engines work, their algorithms and the use of metadata to retrieve information, and applies this knowledge to designing new search and cataloguing strategies; and indicator 2. Evaluates quality models for assessing digital educational content and proposes new models or improvements to existing ones to better suit educational practice.
Area: Teaching and learning
  • A1 for competence 3.1. Teaching because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Knows different pedagogical models and approaches to integrating digital technologies that are consistent with those models for teaching; indicator 2. Selectively integrates digital resources into lesson planning according to their suitability for the objectives, content, students, etc.; and indicator 3. Knows the basic features of different digital educational resources and their possible uses in teaching, and uses them in simulated face-to-face or online situations.
  • A2 for competence 3.1. Teaching because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. With help from other teachers, selectively integrates the school’s digital resources into lesson planning according to their suitability for the objectives, learning, students, etc., following the pedagogical model in the school’s educational project; and indicator 2. Implements lesson plans in teaching practice, resolving with help any problems that arise when using digital technologies.
  • B1 for competence 3.1. Teaching because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Selectively integrates the school’s available digital resources into lesson planning, following the pedagogical model in the educational project; indicator 2. Uses the school’s digital resources conventionally and independently, selecting them according to their features, the educational context and the teaching mode (face-to-face, online, distance, hybrid or blended); indicator 3. While using familiar digital resources, assesses their suitability for helping students achieve learning objectives; and indicator 4. Resolves the most common problems arising when integrating digital technologies into teaching and handles unexpected situations with alternative solutions.
  • B2 for competence 3.1. Teaching because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Transfers innovative practices in the educational use of digital technologies to their teaching context, making the necessary adaptations, and adapts previously used digital resources to new learning situations; indicator 2. Integrates digital technologies into planning and teaching so that students must use them in varied, diverse, selective and responsible ways to complete the proposed activities and achieve learning objectives; indicator 3. Resolves technical and pedagogical problems arising in teaching through well-established theoretical and practical knowledge of both general technologies and those specific to the subject or area taught; and indicator 4. Provides informal support to other teachers in implementing digital technologies in the classroom or planning their integration into teaching.
  • C1 for competence 3.1. Teaching because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Researches new strategies for integrating digital resources into planning and teaching, both in the classroom and across the school; indicator 2. Coordinates or leads the design of strategies for integrating digital technologies in the school and aligning them with the educational project and digital plan or strategy, including pedagogical, teaching and technical aspects; indicator 3. Coordinates or collaborates in configuring and administering the school’s digital technologies; and indicator 4. Coordinates school-based training activities to analyse the inclusion of digital technologies in the pedagogical models established in the educational project.
  • C2 for competence 3.1. Teaching because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Creates new models for integrating digital resources into teaching, developing new educational experiences that significantly improve learning; and indicator 2. Coordinates or develops research projects on the impact of digital technology use on learning.
Area: Assessment and feedback
  • A1 for competence 4.1. Assessment strategies because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Knows and configures the most common digital tools according to the different functions of teaching and learning assessment (diagnostic, formative and summative); indicator 2. Designs assessment activities that students complete using digital media; and indicator 3. Knows personal data protection regulations and how they affect information-gathering processes using digital technologies.
  • A2 for competence 4.1. Assessment strategies because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. With guidance, applies the digital assessment technologies provided by the education authority or school owners to collect information on the indicators established in lesson planning; indicator 2. Under supervision, uses the school’s digital technologies to design a varied range of assessment methods (students’ attitudes, work and performance) that allow learning to be monitored appropriately and possible student needs to be identified; indicator 3. With help from other teachers, designs and uses a tool to evaluate their teaching practice using the school’s digital technologies; and indicator 4. Knows and applies, under supervision, the school’s data protection protocol in assessment procedures involving digital technologies.
  • B1 for competence 4.1. Assessment strategies because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Independently uses the digital assessment platforms provided by the education authority or school owners; indicator 2. Diversifies the techniques, methods and tools for assessing students’ learning and their own teaching practice by independently using the school’s digital technologies; and indicator 3. Independently applies the school’s security and personal data protection protocols in assessment processes.
  • B2 for competence 4.1. Assessment strategies because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Combines techniques, methods and tools for collecting digital data on assessment indicators so that the results can be cross-checked through triangulation; and indicator 2. Applies the school’s digital technologies to designing methods and tools that facilitate the assessment of teaching and learning processes involving new teaching strategies.
  • C1 for competence 4.1. Assessment strategies because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Participates in monitoring and evaluating the protocols and digital technologies used by the school to assess teaching and learning, contributing to their revision or the implementation of new strategies; indicator 2. Advises or trains colleagues in using the school’s digital technologies for educational assessment; and indicator 3. Coordinates the integration of digital technologies into the evaluation of the school’s programmes and projects.
  • C2 for competence 4.1. Assessment strategies because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Researches and critically analyses the functions of digital technologies, including emerging ones, that facilitate data collection to assess teaching and learning processes or different aspects of the education system; and indicator 2. Makes innovative proposals for integrating digital technologies, including emerging ones, into educational assessment, respecting the digital rights and safeguards of everyone involved and aligning with the ethical and pedagogical principles in current education laws.
Area: Empowering learners
  • A1 for competence 5.1. Accessibility and inclusion because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Understands how technological resources available in education support universal accessibility and how to integrate them into teaching practice; indicator 2. Understands the positive and negative effects of including digital technologies in teaching and learning; and indicator 3. Knows the principles of universal accessibility and the educational application of digital technologies to include all students, as well as the relevant current regulations.
  • A2 for competence 5.1. Accessibility and inclusion because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Selects and uses basic accessibility options in the school’s technology in controlled environments or with guidance; and indicator 2. Knows the protocols and measures adopted by the school and/or education authority to reduce the digital divide and applies them with guidance from other teachers.
  • B1 for competence 5.1. Accessibility and inclusion because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Independently uses the accessibility options of the school’s technology, selecting those most appropriate for their students; and indicator 2. Collaborates in implementing measures adopted by the education authority and the school to address the digital divide and promote the educational inclusion of all students in the use of digital technologies.
  • B2 for competence 5.1. Accessibility and inclusion because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Evaluates the accessibility options of the school’s available digital technologies to use them selectively and adapt them to the teaching and learning context; and indicator 2. Adapts technological solutions for inclusion in any educational context and teaching and learning situation, enabling all students to participate and progress in the same teaching process.
  • C1 for competence 5.1. Accessibility and inclusion because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Analyses and evaluates the school’s digital technologies as tools for promoting student accessibility and inclusion, proposing improvements so all students can participate in the same teaching process; indicator 2. Actively collaborates in or coordinates the development and evaluation of pedagogical strategies that enable all students to participate together in teaching and learning using digital technologies; and indicator 3. Provides formal advice or training to other teachers on using digital technologies to facilitate accessibility and inclusion for all students in teaching and learning.
  • C2 for competence 5.1. Accessibility and inclusion because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Researches how accessibility and inclusion aspects of digital technologies improve teaching and learning processes, and proposes new pedagogical strategies; and indicator 2. Collaborates in developing new digital technology functions to improve accessibility and educational inclusion.
Area: Facilitating learners’ digital competence
  • A1 for competence 6.1. Media, information and data literacy because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Knows and understands how browsers, search engines, online services and IoT (Internet of Things) devices operate when searching for, processing and retrieving information and data; and indicator 2. Knows the teaching criteria required to help students become competent in searching for, selecting, evaluating and processing relevant, appropriate and reliable information and data, and how this competence is integrated into the curriculum or programme of study.
  • A2 for competence 6.1. Media, information and data literacy because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. With help from other teachers, applies teaching proposals that integrate the content, activities and approaches needed to develop students’ media, information and data literacy, adapting them to the curriculum, educational project and school digital plan; and indicator 2. Applies technical knowledge of content management and the configuration of information search and processing tools to the use of digital technologies provided by the education authority or school owners.
  • B1 for competence 6.1. Media, information and data literacy because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Integrates learning situations into teaching in which students must develop different strategies for searching for, evaluating, selecting and organising information and data; and indicator 2. Selects the most suitable technologies from those provided by the education authority or school owners to develop students’ competence in handling information and data.
  • B2 for competence 6.1. Media, information and data literacy because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Reflects on and evaluates their own practice to design or adapt new pedagogical proposals that help students develop the ability to determine what information they need, how to search for it, select it critically and organise it; and indicator 2. Configures and uses the digital technologies provided by the education authority or school owners in varied and flexible ways so students develop their competence in handling information and data.
  • C1 for competence 6.1. Media, information and data literacy because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Coordinates or contributes to designing and implementing the pedagogical proposals in the school’s digital plan to develop students’ digital competence in media, information and data literacy, and to evaluating their impact on this learning; indicator 2. Evaluates the digital technologies and services used by the school to develop students’ media, information and data literacy in order to propose improvements; and indicator 3. Advises or trains other teachers on pedagogical strategies and the configuration and use of technologies to strengthen students’ digital competence in media, information and data literacy.
  • C2 for competence 6.1. Media, information and data literacy because it contributes to digital competence development through indicator(s): indicator 1. Researches the impact of the teaching and pedagogical strategies, technologies and digital services commonly used to develop students’ media, information and data literacy; and indicator 2. Uses research to design new pedagogical proposals to improve the acquisition and development of students’ digital competence in media, information and data literacy.

  • There are also buttons for full screen, clearing the selection and previewing the selected items.

Ferredoxin is a small iron-containing protein that acts as an electron acceptor associated with Photosystem I in photosynthesis. It accepts an electron and is reduced, enabling it to transfer those electrons as part of the electron transport process. The NADP+ reductase catalyses the reaction in which ferredoxin is oxidised and NADP+ is reduced to NADPH. NADPH stores energy as a reduced coenzyme, contributing to the Calvin cycle as the main source of reducing power.

The cell wall is a strong, rigid layer that withstands osmotic forces and growth and is located outside the plasma membrane in cells of plants, fungi, algae, bacteria and archaea. The cell wall protects the cell’s contents, provides rigidity, mediates all interactions between the cell and its surroundings, and acts as a cellular compartment. In fungi and plants, it also defines the structure and supports tissues and many other parts of the cell.

The cell wall is made from different materials depending on the type of organism. In plants, the cell wall consists mainly of a polymer of carbohydrate called cellulose, an polysaccharide, and can also act as a carbohydrate store for the cell. In bacteria, the cell wall consists of peptidoglucan. Among archaea there are cell walls with different chemical compositions, including S-layers of glycoproteins, pseudopeptidoglycan or polysaccharides. Fungi have cell walls made of chitin, and algae typically have walls made from glycoproteins and polysaccharides. However, some algal species may have a cell wall composed of silicon dioxide. Other accessory molecules are often integrated into the cell wall.
