Ferredoxin is a small iron-containing protein that acts as an electron acceptor associated with Photosystem I in photosynthesis. It accepts an electron and is reduced, enabling it to transfer those electrons as part of the electron transport process. The NADP+ reductase catalyses the reaction in which ferredoxin is oxidised and NADP+ is reduced to NADPH. NADPH stores energy as a reduced coenzyme, contributing to the Calvin cycle as the main source of reducing power.

The cytoplasm is the part of the protoplasm in a eukaryotic or prokaryotic cell located between the cell nucleus and the plasma membrane. It consists of a very fine, granular-looking colloidal dispersion, the cytosol or hyaloplasm, and a variety of cellular organelles with different functions.

Its function is to house the cellular organelles and contribute to their movement. Many of the cell’s metabolic processes take place in the cytosol.

The cytoplasm is sometimes divided into an outer gelatinous region close to the membrane and involved in cell movement, called the ectoplasm, and a more fluid inner region called the endoplasm, where most organelles are found. Cytoplasm occurs in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells and contains nutrients that have crossed the plasma membrane and thus reached the cell’s organelles.

It's an external, viscous layer with a thickness ranging from 100 to 400 Å. It is very common in pathogenic bacteria because it facilitates adhesion to the host’s tissues. It is not present in all prokaryotes.

That capsule is rich in polysaccharides and protein molecules.

The bacterial capsule has the following functions:

  • Attaches the pathogenic bacterium to its host.
  • Protects the bacterium from the drying of the environment.
  • Regulates the exchange of water and nutrients and also serves as a nutrient store.
  • Defence against antibodies, bacteriophages and phagocytic cells.
  • It allows the formation of colonies of bacteria.

Selecting “Map” from the iDevices list displays a series of options and tabs in eXeLearning:

At the top, we can change the iDevice’s title and assign an icon. There are several tabs, each with a different function, allowing us to configure the game flexibly.

General settings


The “General settings” tab appears by default when creating a Map iDevice.

In this tab, we define the game instructions, the available settings and assessment options, and the activities and interactive areas of the image we use

  • Clicking the “Instructions” opens a text box where we can enter the instructions to follow.
  • Clicking the “Options” section lets us choose the activity or assessment type for the map we are creating: Visited points, Identify, Search, Identify points, Quiz and Order.
  • In the “Map” section, after selecting the assessment/activity type, we can:
    • Enter an image.
    • Add an icon to the image that displays information as text, an image, video, audio, a presentation or another map or interactive image. Add a new point to the map by clicking + 
    • If we select the Quiz activity/assessment type, a new field appears for creating Select, Order or Word questions, similar to those in the Select iDevice.

Passwords

In the “Passwords” tab, we can create a sequence of challenges in which players cannot access a new game until they obtain a key from a previous activity. We can set an access code and a message shown to players when they reach a specified percentage of correct answers, which they can use as the password for a new challenge or subsequent activity. 

Both are optional, and their settings only appear when we enable them, as shown in the image.

Grading

  • SCORM: lets us save the score automatically or using a button, or choose not to save it. The available options depend on the iDevice.
  • Progress report: includes the activity in the report and shows its identifier.
  • Minimum score to pass the activity: uses the project’s global value or lets you select “Custom”.

Saving scores through SCORM requires exporting the content as SCORM and publishing it on a compatible platform, such as Moodle.

Custom texts

This tab lets us customise the text and automatic messages generated by the iDevice.

We can mark areas on the image using different types of icons. Clicking them lets students explore further information through text, images, videos, audio, presentations or new image maps, with unlimited nesting

Students answer a series of questions by identifying the answers on icons placed on the image or map

Students answer a series of questions by identifying the answers in hidden areas of the image or map

Each icon on the image or map presents students with a series of questions.

Students must explore a minimum amount of the map’s content before they can answer the questions.

Students must click the points on the map in the order specified in the instructions

Students must click the points on the map in the order specified in the instructions

Selecting “Guess” from the iDevices list displays several options

At the top, we can change the title and assign an icon. There are several options and tabs, each with a different function, allowing us to configure the game flexibly 

General settings


The “General settings” tab appears by default when creating a Guess iDevice.

In this tab, we define the activities in the iDevice, the game instructions, the settings and options, and the definitions of the words or expressions our students should know.

  • Clicking “Instructions” opens a text box where we can enter the instructions to follow.
  • Clicking “Options” lets us set the maximum time students have to answer each question, the percentage of letters to show, whether to show the answers to each question, whether to shuffle questions each time, the scoring system and whether to display the iDevice minimised. We can also choose whether to use Digital Whiteboard mode. The Progress report is configured in “Grading”.
  • In the Words/Expressions section, we can enter words and expressions with their definitions and optionally include audio, video or images. There are four multimedia options: None, Image, Video and Text.

If you insert a video, the steps are:

  1. Enter the video URL to insert
  2. Click Play to start the video (the video time appears on the grey button)
  3. Play only a section of the video. To do this:
    1. To set the start time, pause the video at the exact point where you want it to begin (the time appears on the grey button). Then click “Start” (it will have a blue border) and click the grey time button. 
    2. To set the end time, pause the video at the exact point where you want it to finish (the time appears on the grey button). Then click “Start” (it will have a blue border) and click the grey time button. 
  4. We can also mute part of the video by specifying its start time and duration.

Passwords

In the “Passwords” tab, we can create a sequence of challenges in which players cannot access a new game until they obtain a key from a previous activity. We can set an access code and a message shown to players when they reach a specified percentage of correct answers, which they can use as the password for a new challenge or subsequent activity. 

Both are optional, and their settings only appear when we enable them, as shown in the image.

Grading

  • SCORM: lets us save the score automatically or using a button, or choose not to save it. The available options depend on the iDevice.
  • Progress report: includes the activity in the report and shows its identifier.
  • Minimum score to pass the activity: uses the project’s global value or lets you select “Custom”.

Saving scores through SCORM requires exporting the content as SCORM and publishing it on a compatible platform, such as Moodle.

Custom texts

This tab lets us customise the text and automatic messages generated by the iDevice.

Import / Export

On the "Import / Export" tab we can import questions compatible with this activity from TXT or XML (Moodle) files, or we can export questions in txt format to integrate them into other compatible activities.

AI

This tab makes it easy to import questions from an AI chatbot. It shows an example prompt that we can take to a chatbot to generate questions in the correct format for pasting into the “Questions” tab. When we save, the AI-generated questions are added to the iDevice, ready to use in the activity.

odeComponent.htmlView:
Selecting “Adaptative Quiz” from the iDevices list displays several options

At the top, we can change the title and assign an icon. Several options and tabs have different functions, allowing us to configure the game flexibly

General settings

The “General settings” tab appears by default when creating a Form iDevice.

In this tab, we define the activities in the iDevice, the instructions and options, and the questions students must answer in this form.

  • Clicking “Instructions” opens a text box where we can enter the instructions to follow.
  • Clicking “Options” lets us configure the time, levels and number of questions, among other settings. The Progress report is configured in “Grading”.
  • In the “Questions” section, we can add questions as needed, of the type Select, Order or Word. We can choose whether to add multimedia, the number of options and whether the questions are “Easy”, “Medium” or “Hard”.

Passwords

You can create a sequence of challenges in which players cannot access a new game or challenge until they obtain a key from a previous activity. Set an access code and a message shown to players when they reach a specified percentage of correct answers, which they can use as the password for a new challenge or subsequent activity.

Grading

  • SCORM: lets us save the score automatically or using a button, or choose not to save it. The available options depend on the iDevice.
  • Progress report: includes the activity in the report and shows its identifier.
  • Minimum score to pass the activity: uses the project’s global value or lets you select “Custom”.

Saving scores through SCORM requires exporting the content as SCORM and publishing it on a compatible platform, such as Moodle.

Custom texts

This tab lets us customise the text and automatic messages generated by the iDevice.

Import / Export

On the "Import / Export" tab we can import questions compatible with this activity from TXT or XML (Moodle) files, or we can export questions in txt format to integrate them into other compatible activities.

AI

This tab makes it easy to import questions from an AI chatbot. It shows an example prompt that we can take to a chatbot to generate questions in the correct format for pasting into the “Questions” tab. When we save, the AI-generated questions are added to the iDevice, ready to use in the activity.

odeComponent.htmlView:
We use this iDevice to ask questions in several formats, which can all be combined in the same “Form”. These are:

  • To create questions that will have to be answered with “True” or “False”. 
  • To give students a text with gaps that they must fill in. (“Fill in the gaps" ).
  • To give students a text with a list of possible word strings to select from. We can add new words (separated by “|” in the corresponding box) to increase the possible answers. (“Dropdown”)
  • To set one (or several) multiple-choice questions (“Selection”) to students. Each question can have only one correct answer (“Single”) or several (“Multiple")

with this iDevice we can add a checklist with a structured, easy-to-understand list of the activities proposed throughout the educational resource. This is a useful tool for students to regulate their own learning by tracking the activities they complete.

We can configure the checklist with sections and subsections so students can mark completed activities, select an activity’s status from a dropdown or enter text. When finished, they can download the report as a PNG image.

Incompatible browser

Selecting “Progress report” from the iDevices list displays the following in eXeLearning:

At the top, we can change the title and assign an icon. Several options and tabs have different functions for configuring the checklist.

General settings

In “Options”, enter the checklist’s title and subtitle. We can configure options to show user details, remember selected options, assign scores, include a logo or decorative images, and more. The checklist can include different types of activities:

  • Box: Displays a checkbox for students to tick when they have completed the specified activity
  • Text: Displays a checkbox for students to tick when they have completed the specified activity and a text box for entering content.
  • Select: Students select from a dropdown whether the activity is completed, in progress or incomplete.
  • Do not mark: Displays text only, with no option to tick a box or enter content. This is recommended for section or subsection headings, for example.

Custom texts

This tab lets us customise the text and automatic messages generated by the iDevice.

  • Activity

  • Date
  • Score
  • Notes
  • Restart
  • Print
  • Apply
  • New window

We can create a rubric from scratch or load one of the examples provided in eXeLearning.

Grading

  • SCORM: lets us save the score automatically or using a button, or choose not to save it. The available options depend on the iDevice.
  • Progress report: includes the activity in the report and shows its identifier.
  • Minimum score to pass the activity: uses the project’s global value or lets you select “Custom”.

Saving scores through SCORM requires exporting the content as SCORM and publishing it on a compatible platform, such as Moodle.

In either case, we will be able to customize all parameters:

  • The rubric title
  • The issues to be assessed
  • Performance levels
  • The descriptors
  • The weight of each descriptor

Also change order and remove columns    and rows  and add new . Finally, we can add or edit information about the rubric’s authorship and licence.

Once created, the rubric can be used to assess students and print the assessments.

The process for using the Rubric iDevice is described below.

New rubric

Selecting “New rubric” starts with a 4×4 table that we can complete and customise.

Sample rubrics

Selecting “Example rubrics” lets us choose one of several examples (oral presentation, video, infographic, etc.) and adapt it. All fields can be edited.

Use

Once the rubric has been created, we can fill in the Activity, Student name and Date fields, select the relevant rubric cells and download the result as a PDF.

Selecting “Select” from the iDevices list displays the following in eXeLearning:

At the top, we can change the title and assign an icon. Several options and tabs have different functions, allowing us to configure the game flexibly

General settings

The “General settings” tab appears by default when creating a Select iDevice.

In this tab, we define the activities in the iDevice, instructions for completing them, settings and options, and the definitions of the words or expressions our students should know.

  • Clicking “Instructions” opens a text box where we can enter the instructions to follow.
  • Clicking “Options” lets us set the maximum time students have to answer each question, the percentage of letters, whether to show the solution for each question (and play audio when showing it), whether to shuffle questions each time, and the scoring system. The Progress report is configured in “Grading”.
  • In the Questions section, we can:
    • Choose the game type: select several answers (Select), arrange the answers (Order) or guess a word (Word).
    • For the first two types, as in other games, we can choose the multimedia type, number of options and time per question.
    • If we choose “Word” as the game type, we can set the percentage of letters to show and the time allowed for the question.

Passwords

In the “Passwords” tab, we can create a sequence of challenges in which players cannot access a new game until they obtain a key from a previous activity. We can set an access code and a message shown to players when they reach a specified percentage of correct answers, which they can use as the password for a new challenge or subsequent activity. 

Both are optional, and their settings only appear when we enable them, as shown in the image.

Grading

  • SCORM: lets us save the score automatically or using a button, or choose not to save it. The available options depend on the iDevice.
  • Progress report: includes the activity in the report and shows its identifier.
  • Minimum score to pass the activity: uses the project’s global value or lets you select “Custom”.

Saving scores through SCORM requires exporting the content as SCORM and publishing it on a compatible platform, such as Moodle.

Custom texts

This tab lets us customise the text and automatic messages generated by the iDevice.

Import / Export

On the "Import / Export" tab we can import questions compatible with this activity from TXT or XML (Moodle) files, or we can export questions in txt format to integrate them into other compatible activities.

AI

This tab makes it easy to import questions from an AI chatbot. It shows an example prompt that we can take to a chatbot to generate questions in the correct format for pasting into the “Questions” tab. When we save, the AI-generated questions are added to the iDevice, ready to use in the activity.

Selecting “Select media files” from the iDevices list displays the following in eXeLearning:

At the top, we can change the title and assign an icon. Several options and tabs have different functions, allowing us to configure the game flexibly

General settings


The “General settings” tab appears by default when creating a “Select media files” iDevice.

In this tab, we define the game instructions, available options and settings, and questions with the clues we choose.

  • Clicking “Instructions” opens a text box where we can enter the instructions to follow.
  • Clicking “Options” lets us choose whether to display the game minimised, its duration, the number of attempts, whether to show solutions, how long the cards remain visible, the percentage of all cards to show in each round and the maximum number of cards. We can also define custom messages, display cards in table mode and show feedback (including the score required for it to appear). The Progress report is configured in “Grading”.
  • In “Activities”, enter the prompt (with an image and/or audio if desired) and each card’s content, indicating whether it is a correct answer:

Passwords

In the “Passwords” tab, we can create a sequence of challenges in which players cannot access a new game until they obtain a key from a previous activity. We can set an access code and a message shown to players when they reach a specified percentage of correct answers, which they can use as the password for a new challenge or subsequent activity. 

Both are optional, and their settings only appear when we enable them, as shown in the image.

Grading

  • SCORM: lets us save the score automatically or using a button, or choose not to save it. The available options depend on the iDevice.
  • Progress report: includes the activity in the report and shows its identifier.
  • Minimum score to pass the activity: uses the project’s global value or lets you select “Custom”.

Saving scores through SCORM requires exporting the content as SCORM and publishing it on a compatible platform, such as Moodle.

Custom texts

This tab lets us customise the text and automatic messages generated by the iDevice.

Selecting “Test” from the iDevices list displays the following in eXeLearning:

At the top, we can change the title and assign an icon. Several options and tabs have different functions, allowing us to configure the game flexibly 

General settings

The “General settings” tab appears by default when creating a “Test” iDevice.

In this tab, we define the activities in the iDevice, the game instructions, settings and options, and the questions we will ask students.

  • Clicking the “Instructions” link opens a text box where we can enter the instructions to follow.
  • Clicking “Options” lets us configure how the iDevice is displayed, the number of lives, the scoring system, whether to shuffle questions and answers, and whether to show solutions after questions have been answered. We can include an introductory video at the start of the activity. The Progress report is configured in “Grading”.
  • The “Questions” link lets us create questions with supporting multimedia, choose up to four possible answers (only one is correct) and set the maximum time allowed to answer. The four options are: Without multimedia, Image, Video and Text.

    If a video, the steps are:

    1. Enter the video URL to insert
    2. Click Play to start the video (the video time appears on the grey button)
    3. Play only a section of the video. To do this:
      1. To set the start time, pause the video at the exact point where you want it to begin (the time appears on the grey button). Then click “Start” (it will have a blue border) and click the grey time button. 
      2. To set the end time, pause the video at the exact point where you want it to finish (the time appears on the grey button). Then click “Start” (it will have a blue border) and click the grey time button. 
    4. We can also mute part of the video by specifying its start time and duration

Using icons  we can create new questions, access existing questions to edit them, and delete, copy or cut questions.

Passwords

In the “Passwords” tab, we can create a sequence of challenges in which players cannot access a new game or challenge until they obtain a key from a previous activity. We can set an access code and a message shown to players when they reach a specified percentage of correct answers, which they can use as the password for a new challenge or subsequent activity.

Both are optional, and their settings only appear when we enable them, as shown in the image.

Grading

  • SCORM: lets us save the score automatically or using a button, or choose not to save it. The available options depend on the iDevice.
  • Progress report: includes the activity in the report and shows its identifier.
  • Minimum score to pass the activity: uses the project’s global value or lets you select “Custom”.

Saving scores through SCORM requires exporting the content as SCORM and publishing it on a compatible platform, such as Moodle.

Custom texts

This tab lets us customise the text and automatic messages generated by the iDevice.

Import / Export

On the "Import / Export" tab we can import questions compatible with this activity from TXT or XML (Moodle) files, or we can export questions in txt format to integrate them into other compatible activities.

AI

This tab makes it easy to import questions from an AI chatbot. It shows an example prompt that we can take to a chatbot to generate questions in the correct format for pasting into the “Questions” tab. When we save, the AI-generated questions are added to the iDevice, ready to use in the activity.

  • Clicking the “Instructions” link opens a text box where we can enter the instructions to follow.
  • Clicking “Options” lets us configure how the iDevice is displayed, the number of lives, the scoring system, whether to shuffle questions and answers, and whether to show solutions after questions have been answered. We can include an introductory video at the start of the activity. The Progress report is configured in “Grading”.
  • The “Questions” link lets us create questions with supporting multimedia, choose up to four possible answers (only one is correct) and set the maximum time allowed to answer. The four options are: Without multimedia, Image, Video and Text.

    If a video, the steps are:

    1. Enter the video URL to insert
    2. Click Play to start the video (the video time appears on the grey button)
    3. Play only a section of the video. To do this:
      1. To set the start time, pause the video at the exact point where you want it to begin (the time appears on the grey button). Then click “Start” (it will have a blue border) and click the grey time button. 
      2. To set the end time, pause the video at the exact point where you want it to finish (the time appears on the grey button). Then click “Start” (it will have a blue border) and click the grey time button. 
    4. We can also mute part of the video by specifying its start time and duration

Using icons  we can create new questions, access existing questions to edit them, and delete, copy or cut questions.

Passwords

In the “Passwords” tab, we can create a sequence of challenges in which players cannot access a new game or challenge until they obtain a key from a previous activity. We can set an access code and a message shown to players when they reach a specified percentage of correct answers, which they can use as the password for a new challenge or subsequent activity.

Both are optional, and their settings only appear when we enable them, as shown in the image.

Grading

  • SCORM: lets us save the score automatically or using a button, or choose not to save it. The available options depend on the iDevice.
  • Progress report: includes the activity in the report and shows its identifier.
  • Minimum score to pass the activity: uses the project’s global value or lets you select “Custom”.

Saving scores through SCORM requires exporting the content as SCORM and publishing it on a compatible platform, such as Moodle.

Custom texts

This tab lets us customise the text and automatic messages generated by the iDevice.

Import / Export

On the "Import / Export" tab we can import questions compatible with this activity from TXT or XML (Moodle) files, or we can export questions in txt format to integrate them into other compatible activities.

AI

This tab makes it easy to import questions from an AI chatbot. It shows an example prompt that we can take to a chatbot to generate questions in the correct format for pasting into the “Questions” tab. When we save, the AI-generated questions are added to the iDevice, ready to use in the activity.

Selecting “Video test” from the iDevices list displays the following in eXeLearning:

At the top, we can change the title and assign an icon. Several options and tabs have different functions, allowing us to configure the game flexibly 

General settings


The “General settings” tab is displayed by default when you create the Video test iDevice.

In this tab, we define the activities in the iDevice, instructions for playing the game, the various settings and options, and the questions associated with the video our students will watch.

  • Clicking the “Instructions” link opens a text box where we can enter the instructions to follow.
  • Clicking the “Options” link lets us configure whether to display solutions randomly, how long the solution is displayed, the scoring system, the number of lives and whether to minimise the iDevice. The Progress report is configured in “Grading”.
  • The Questions link lets us add a YouTube video or a file, write the questions and decide at which second they will appear for our students. The steps have to be:
    1. Enter the video URL to insert
    2. Click the Play button to start the video (the video time will appear in the grey button below the viewer).
    3. Play only a section of the video. To do this:
      1. To set the start time, pause the video at the exact point where you want it to begin (the time appears on the grey button). Then click “Start” (it will have a blue border) and click the grey time button. 
      2. To set the end time, pause the video at the exact point where you want it to finish (the time appears on the grey button). Then click “Start” (it will have a blue border) and click the grey time button. 
    4. To add a question at a specific point, follow the same procedure, this time selecting the “Question point” field.
    5. We can also mute part of the video by specifying its start time and duration.
    Using icons  We can navigate our questions, add new or remove them.

Passwords

In the “Passwords” tab, we can create a sequence of challenges in which players cannot access a new game or challenge until they obtain a key from a previous activity. We can set an access code and a message shown to players when they reach a specified percentage of correct answers, which they can use as the password for a new challenge or subsequent activity.

Both are optional, and their settings only appear when we enable them, as shown in the image.

Grading

  • SCORM: lets us save the score automatically or using a button, or choose not to save it. The available options depend on the iDevice.
  • Progress report: includes the activity in the report and shows its identifier.
  • Minimum score to pass the activity: uses the project’s global value or lets you select “Custom”.

Saving scores through SCORM requires exporting the content as SCORM and publishing it on a compatible platform, such as Moodle.

Selecting “Video test” from the iDevices list displays the following in eXeLearning:

At the top, we can change the title and assign an icon. Several options and tabs have different functions, allowing us to configure the game flexibly 

General settings


The “General settings” tab is displayed by default when you create the Video test iDevice.

In this tab, we define the activities in the iDevice, instructions for playing the game, the various settings and options, and the questions associated with the video our students will watch.

  • Clicking the “Instructions” link opens a text box where we can enter the instructions to follow.
  • Clicking the “Options” link lets us configure whether to display solutions randomly, how long the solution is displayed, the scoring system, the number of lives and whether to minimise the iDevice. The Progress report is configured in “Grading”.
  • The Questions link lets us add a YouTube video or a file, write the questions and decide at which second they will appear for our students. The steps have to be:
    1. Enter the video URL to insert
    2. Click the Play button to start the video (the video time will appear in the grey button below the viewer).
    3. Play only a section of the video. To do this:
      1. To set the start time, pause the video at the exact point where you want it to begin (the time appears on the grey button). Then click “Start” (it will have a blue border) and click the grey time button. 
      2. To set the end time, pause the video at the exact point where you want it to finish (the time appears on the grey button). Then click “Start” (it will have a blue border) and click the grey time button. 
    4. To add a question at a specific point, follow the same procedure, this time selecting the “Question point” field.
    5. We can also mute part of the video by specifying its start time and duration.
    Using icons  We can navigate our questions, add new or remove them.

Passwords

In the “Passwords” tab, we can create a sequence of challenges in which players cannot access a new game or challenge until they obtain a key from a previous activity. We can set an access code and a message shown to players when they reach a specified percentage of correct answers, which they can use as the password for a new challenge or subsequent activity.

Both are optional, and their settings only appear when we enable them, as shown in the image.

Grading

  • SCORM: lets us save the score automatically or using a button, or choose not to save it. The available options depend on the iDevice.
  • Progress report: includes the activity in the report and shows its identifier.
  • Minimum score to pass the activity: uses the project’s global value or lets you select “Custom”.

Saving scores through SCORM requires exporting the content as SCORM and publishing it on a compatible platform, such as Moodle.

Custom texts

This tab lets us customise the text and automatic messages generated by the iDevice.

Selecting the iDevice “Interactive video” from the list of iDevices displays the following in eXeLearning:

Grading

  • SCORM: lets us save the score automatically or using a button, or choose not to save it. The available options depend on the iDevice.
  • Progress report: includes the activity in the report and shows its identifier.
  • Minimum score to pass the activity: uses the project’s global value or lets you select “Custom”.

Saving scores through SCORM requires exporting the content as SCORM and publishing it on a compatible platform, such as Moodle.

Let us look at the contents of these tabs in the Interactive video iDevice:

The video editor

Once we have configured the video source to which we want to add interactivity, we open the video editor, which looks like this:

It contains two sections of options. The options for saving and leaving the editor are at the top right, and below, to the right of the video, are the following options:

Help: shows brief information about each of the editor’s options.

To create a cover: lets us set a title and a short introduction or an image to serve as the video cover. An image can also be included instead of text.

Creating a frame: lets us insert a frame alongside the video to display information or create an activity for the user.

The tool is very versatile and lets us create frames of 8 different types:

Text

At the top right we have a Help button which tells us:

  • Specify the second at which the frame should appear (Start)
  • If you do not want the video to stop, specify when the frame should be hidden (End)
  • Click to get the current second
  • Text: Write some text. You can add lists, links...

Note: The timing settings are similar for the other frame categories, except those that require user action, where stopping the video is mandatory.

Image

Very similar to the text type in how it works, but it only allows us to insert an image, which will appear at the specified time. The end user will see the image and can open it in a new browser window.

Selecting “Word search” from the iDevices list displays the following in eXeLearning:

At the top, we can change the title and assign an icon. Several options and tabs have different functions, allowing us to configure the game flexibly 

General settings


The “General settings” tab is displayed by default when you create the Word search iDevice.

In this tab, we define the instructions for playing the game, the various available options and settings, and the questions.

  • Clicking the “Instructions” opens a text box where we can enter the instructions to follow.
  • Clicking the “Options” lets us decide whether to display the game minimised, the time, whether to show the solve button, whether to allow diagonal and reversed words, specific feedback at the end of the game if a certain percentage of correct answers has been reached, and the number of questions to display in the game. The Progress report is configured in “Grading”.
  • In the “Words / Phrases” section, we can enter the following for each:
    • The word to find in the word search and its definition, which will appear beside the game.
    • A related image.
    • An audio describing the word

Passwords

In the “Passwords” lets us create a sequence of challenges in which players cannot access a new game until they obtain a key in a previous activity. To do this, we can set an access code and a message that appears when players reach a set percentage of correct answers, which they can use as the password for a new challenge or a later activity. 

Both are optional, and their settings only appear when we enable them, as shown in the image.

Grading

  • SCORM: lets us save the score automatically or using a button, or choose not to save it. The available options depend on the iDevice.
  • Progress report: includes the activity in the report and shows its identifier.
  • Minimum score to pass the activity: uses the project’s global value or lets you select “Custom”.

Saving scores through SCORM requires exporting the content as SCORM and publishing it on a compatible platform, such as Moodle.

Custom texts

This tab lets us customise the text and automatic messages generated by the iDevice.

Import / Export

In the “Import / Export” tab, we can import questions compatible with this activity from TXT or XML (Moodle) files, or we can export questions in txt format to integrate them into other compatible activities.

AI

This tab makes it easy to import questions from an AI chatbot. It shows an example prompt that we can take to a chatbot to generate questions in the correct format for pasting into the “Questions” tab. When we save, the AI-generated questions are added to the iDevice, ready to use in the activity.

Selecting “Padlock” from the iDevices list displays the following in eXeLearning:

At the top, we can change the title and assign an icon. Several options and tabs have different functions, allowing us to configure the game flexibly

General settings

The “General settings” tab is displayed by default when you create the Padlock iDevice.

In this tab, we provide the activity Instructions and the Feedback to display once the correct access code has been entered. 

We define the access code and the time available to enter it, and can configure whether the activity can be repeated and the number of errors allowed before the error message appears.

    Custom texts

    This tab lets us customise the text and automatic messages generated by the iDevice.

    Grading

    • SCORM: lets us save the score automatically or using a button, or choose not to save it. The available options depend on the iDevice.
    • Progress report: includes the activity in the report and shows its identifier.
    • Minimum score to pass the activity: uses the project’s global value or lets you select “Custom”.

    Saving scores through SCORM requires exporting the content as SCORM and publishing it on a compatible platform, such as Moodle.

Selecting “Crossword” from the iDevices list displays several options:

At the top, we can change the title and assign an icon. There are several options and tabs, each with a different function, allowing us to configure the game flexibly 

General settings

The “General settings” tab is displayed by default when you create the Crossword iDevice.

In this tab, we define the activities in the iDevice, instructions for completing them, settings and options, and the definitions of the words or expressions our students should know.

  • Clicking “Instructions” opens a text box where we can enter the instructions to follow.
  • Clicking the “Options” section lets us configure the maximum time students have to answer each question, the difficulty percentage and whether to show the solutions for each question, among other settings. The Progress report is configured in “Grading”.
  • Under "Words" we have several options:

Passwords

In the “Passwords” tab, we can create a sequence of challenges in which players cannot access a new game until they obtain a key from a previous activity. We can set an access code and a message shown to players when they reach a specified percentage of correct answers, which they can use as the password for a new challenge or subsequent activity. 

Both are optional, and their settings only appear when we enable them, as shown in the image.

Grading

  • SCORM: lets us save the score automatically or using a button, or choose not to save it. The available options depend on the iDevice.
  • Progress report: includes the activity in the report and shows its identifier.
  • Minimum score to pass the activity: uses the project’s global value or lets you select “Custom”.

Saving scores through SCORM requires exporting the content as SCORM and publishing it on a compatible platform, such as Moodle.

Custom texts

This tab lets us customise the text and automatic messages generated by the iDevice.

Import / Export

On the "Import / Export" tab we can import questions compatible with this activity from TXT or XML (Moodle) files, or we can export questions in txt format to integrate them into other compatible activities.

AI

This tab makes it easy to import questions from an AI chatbot. It shows an example prompt that we can take to a chatbot to generate questions in the correct format for pasting into the “Questions” tab. When we save, the AI-generated questions are added to the iDevice, ready to use in the activity.

Selecting “Challenge” from the iDevices list displays the following in eXeLearning:

At the top, we can change the title and assign an icon. Several options and tabs have different functions, allowing us to configure the game flexibly 

General settings

The “General settings” tab is displayed by default when you create the Challenge iDevice.

In this tab, we define the activities in the iDevice, the game instructions, the settings and options, and the definitions of the words or expressions our students should know.

  • Clicking “Instructions” opens a text box where we can enter the instructions to follow.
  • Clicking the “Options” section lets us choose whether to minimise the iDevice. The Progress report is configured in “Grading”.

  • In the Questions Section we have two tabs: Challenge, which explains the challenge players will face and the time they have to enter the final answer, and Tasks, where we define the intermediate tasks that players must complete. Each task can have up to 3 clues that appear after the time set for each one.


Custom texts

This tab lets us customise the text and automatic messages generated by the iDevice.

Grading

  • SCORM: lets us save the score automatically or using a button, or choose not to save it. The available options depend on the iDevice.
  • Progress report: includes the activity in the report and shows its identifier.
  • Minimum score to pass the activity: uses the project’s global value or lets you select “Custom”.

Saving scores through SCORM requires exporting the content as SCORM and publishing it on a compatible platform, such as Moodle.

We'll use this iDevice to create games in which players have to discover pairs, trios or groups of four cards with images, text and/or sounds.

Depending on the difficulty level, we can create games with different options, for pairs, trios or groups of four:

  • Level beginner: Allows direct play without the intermediate or advanced level option on screen
  • Level intermediate: Allows direct play with the beginner or advanced level option on screen
  • Level advanced: Allows direct play with options for any level on screen.

Selecting “Discover” from the iDevices list displays the following in eXeLearning:

At the top, we can change the title and assign an icon. Several options and tabs have different functions, allowing us to configure the game flexibly 

General settings

The “General settings” tab is displayed by default when you create the Discover iDevice.

In this tab, we define the instructions for playing the game and the various available options and settings.

  • Clicking “Instructions” opens a text box where we can enter the instructions to follow.
  • Clicking the “Options” section lets us decide whether the game starts minimised, choose the game type (pairs, trios or groups of four) and the difficulty level from 1 to 3, keep cards visible for a set time, customise the correct and incorrect answer messages, and set the game time or number of attempts. We can also choose whether to show solutions, set a feedback message, the percentage of questions required to pass the game, and authorship. The Progress report is configured in “Grading”.
  • In the “Pairs” section, depending on whether we have chosen pairs, trios or groups of four, we can enter the following for each:
    • The text / image / audio for the first pair, trio or group of four.
    • The text / image / audio for the second pair, trio or group of four.
    • The same for the third, fourth, etc...

Passwords

In the “Passwords” tab, we can create a sequence of challenges in which players cannot access a new game until they obtain a key from a previous activity. We can set an access code and a message shown to players when they reach a specified percentage of correct answers, which they can use as the password for a new challenge or subsequent activity. 

Both are optional, and their settings only appear when we enable them, as shown in the image.

Grading

  • SCORM: lets us save the score automatically or using a button, or choose not to save it. The available options depend on the iDevice.
  • Progress report: includes the activity in the report and shows its identifier.
  • Minimum score to pass the activity: uses the project’s global value or lets you select “Custom”.

Saving scores through SCORM requires exporting the content as SCORM and publishing it on a compatible platform, such as Moodle.

Custom texts

This tab lets us customise the text and automatic messages generated by the iDevice.

Import / Export

On the "Import / Export" tab we can import questions compatible with this activity from TXT or XML (Moodle) files, or we can export questions in txt format to integrate them into other compatible activities.

AI

This tab makes it easy to import questions from an AI chatbot. It shows an example prompt that we can take to a chatbot to generate questions in the correct format for pasting into the “Questions” tab. When we save, the AI-generated questions are added to the iDevice, ready to use in the activity.

Selecting “Hidden image” from the iDevices list displays the following in eXeLearning:

At the top, we can change the title and assign an icon. Several options and tabs have different functions, allowing us to configure the game flexibly

General settings

The “General settings” tab is displayed by default when you create the Hidden image iDevice.

In this tab, we define the activities in the iDevice, instructions for completing them, settings and options, and the definitions of the words or expressions our students should know.

  • Clicking “Instructions” opens a text box where we can enter the instructions to follow.
  • Clicking “Options” lets us set the maximum time students have to answer each question, the percentage of letters, whether to show the solution for each question (and play audio when showing it), whether to shuffle questions each time, and the scoring system. The Progress report is configured in “Grading”.
  • In the Questions Section we have a number of simple options:

Passwords

In the “Passwords” tab, we can create a sequence of challenges in which players cannot access a new game until they obtain a key from a previous activity. We can set an access code and a message shown to players when they reach a specified percentage of correct answers, which they can use as the password for a new challenge or subsequent activity. 

Both are optional, and their settings only appear when we enable them, as shown in the image.

Grading

  • SCORM: lets us save the score automatically or using a button, or choose not to save it. The available options depend on the iDevice.
  • Progress report: includes the activity in the report and shows its identifier.
  • Minimum score to pass the activity: uses the project’s global value or lets you select “Custom”.

Saving scores through SCORM requires exporting the content as SCORM and publishing it on a compatible platform, such as Moodle.

Custom texts

This tab lets us customise the text and automatic messages generated by the iDevice.

Selecting “Puzzle” from the iDevices list displays the following in eXeLearning:

At the top, we can change the title and assign an icon. Several options and tabs have different functions, allowing us to configure the game flexibly

General settings

The “General settings” tab is displayed by default when you create the Puzzle iDevice.

In this tab, we define the activities in the iDevice, instructions for completing them, settings and options, and the definitions of the words or expressions our students should know.

  • Clicking “Instructions” opens a text box where we can enter the instructions to follow.
  • Clicking the “Options” section lets us configure randomisation, the percentage of activities and feedback. The Progress report is configured in “Grading”.
  • In the Puzzles section, we can:
    • Choose the game type: slide or swap pieces, and choose the number of rows and columns (minimum 2 and maximum 7)
    • Choose whether to display images, numbers, time or attempts.
    • Include the image, prompt and comments or solution, with their corresponding audio.

Passwords

In the “Passwords” tab, we can create a sequence of challenges in which players cannot access a new game until they obtain a key from a previous activity. We can set an access code and a message shown to players when they reach a specified percentage of correct answers, which they can use as the password for a new challenge or subsequent activity. 

Both are optional, and their settings only appear when we enable them, as shown in the image.

Grading

  • SCORM: lets us save the score automatically or using a button, or choose not to save it. The available options depend on the iDevice.
  • Progress report: includes the activity in the report and shows its identifier.
  • Minimum score to pass the activity: uses the project’s global value or lets you select “Custom”.

Saving scores through SCORM requires exporting the content as SCORM and publishing it on a compatible platform, such as Moodle.

Custom texts

This tab lets us customise the text and automatic messages generated by the iDevice.

Selecting “A-Z quiz” from the iDevices list displays the following in eXeLearning:

At the top, we can change the title and assign an icon. Several options and tabs have different functions, allowing us to configure the game flexibly

General settings

The “General settings” tab is displayed by default when you create the A-Z quiz iDevice.

In this tab, we define the activities in the iDevice, the game instructions, the settings and options, and the definitions of the words or expressions our students should know.

  • Clicking the “Instructions” link opens a text box where we can enter the instructions to follow.
  • Clicking the “Options” link lets us configure the maximum time students have to play the game, the number of rounds around the circle, whether to show solutions for each question and whether to minimise the iDevice. The Progress report is configured in “Grading”.
  • The “Words” link lets us enter the words and their definitions. With the icon  the player is asked for the word we have defined that starts with the letter (A, in this case). We can ask for a word containing the letter in the current row, based on its definition, by clicking the icon . Similarly, we can add an image to accompany each word by clicking the icon 

Passwords

In the “Passwords” tab, we can create a sequence of challenges in which players cannot access a new game or challenge until they obtain a key from a previous activity. We can set an access code and a message shown to players when they reach a specified percentage of correct answers, which they can use as the password for a new challenge or subsequent activity.

Both are optional, and their settings only appear when we enable them, as shown in the image.

Grading

  • SCORM: lets us save the score automatically or using a button, or choose not to save it. The available options depend on the iDevice.
  • Progress report: includes the activity in the report and shows its identifier.
  • Minimum score to pass the activity: uses the project’s global value or lets you select “Custom”.

Saving scores through SCORM requires exporting the content as SCORM and publishing it on a compatible platform, such as Moodle.

Custom texts

This tab lets us customise the text and automatic messages generated by the iDevice.

Import / Export

On the "Import / Export" tab we can import questions compatible with this activity from TXT or XML (Moodle) files, or we can export questions in txt format to integrate them into other compatible activities.

AI

This tab makes it easy to import questions from an AI chatbot. It shows an example prompt that we can take to a chatbot to generate questions in the correct format for pasting into the “Questions” tab. When we save, the AI-generated questions are added to the iDevice, ready to use in the activity.

Selecting “TriviExt” from the iDevices list displays the following in eXeLearning:

At the top, we can change the title and assign an icon. Several options and tabs have different functions, allowing us to configure the game flexibly

General settings


The “General settings” tab is displayed by default when you create the TriviExt iDevice.

In this tab, we define the instructions for playing the game, the various available settings and options, and questions in which students select the correct answer or order of answers, or identify expressions and words from a definition.

  • Clicking “Instructions” opens a text box where we can enter the instructions to follow.
  • Clicking the “Options” section lets us configure the number of topics (wedges) into which we will group questions, whether to display the game minimised, and whether to show question solutions for a set time. The Progress report is configured in “Grading”.
  • In the Questions section, we can:
    • Define the names of the topics, categories or “wedges” in which the questions we create later will appear.
    • Choose the game mode: select several answers (Select), order the answers (Order) or guess a word (Word). As with the Select iDevice, we can choose the multimedia element type, the number of options and the time per question. If we choose “Word” as the game mode, we can set the percentage of letters to display and the time for the question.

Remember that questions and their answers are assigned to the topic or category in which we created them. We can switch question topics or categories by clicking the numbered box.

Do not worry if you accidentally create a question in the wrong category. You can copy the question, switch categories and paste it into the correct one! You do not need to write it again.

Passwords

In the “Passwords” tab, we can create a sequence of challenges in which players cannot access a new game until they obtain a key from a previous activity. We can set an access code and a message shown to players when they reach a specified percentage of correct answers, which they can use as the password for a new challenge or subsequent activity. 

Both are optional, and their settings only appear when we enable them, as shown in the image.

Grading

  • SCORM: lets us save the score automatically or using a button, or choose not to save it. The available options depend on the iDevice.
  • Progress report: includes the activity in the report and shows its identifier.
  • Minimum score to pass the activity: uses the project’s global value or lets you select “Custom”.

Saving scores through SCORM requires exporting the content as SCORM and publishing it on a compatible platform, such as Moodle.

Custom texts

This tab lets us customise the text and automatic messages generated by the iDevice.

Selecting “Drag and drop” from the iDevices list displays the following in eXeLearning:

At the top, we can change the title and assign an icon. Several options and tabs have different functions, allowing us to configure the game flexibly

General settings


The “General settings” tab is displayed by default when you create the Drag and drop iDevice.

In this tab, we define the activities in the iDevice, instructions for completing them, settings and options, and the definitions of the words or expressions our students should know.

  • Clicking “Instructions” opens a text box where we can enter the instructions to follow.
  • Clicking the “Options” section lets us configure the font and three difficulty levels (the advanced level has a time limit). The Progress report is configured in “Grading”.
  • The Activities Section will have a number of simple options:

Passwords

In the “Passwords” tab, we can create a sequence of challenges in which players cannot access a new game until they obtain a key from a previous activity. We can set an access code and a message shown to players when they reach a specified percentage of correct answers, which they can use as the password for a new challenge or subsequent activity. 

Both are optional, and their settings only appear when we enable them, as shown in the image.

Grading

  • SCORM: lets us save the score automatically or using a button, or choose not to save it. The available options depend on the iDevice.
  • Progress report: includes the activity in the report and shows its identifier.
  • Minimum score to pass the activity: uses the project’s global value or lets you select “Custom”.

Saving scores through SCORM requires exporting the content as SCORM and publishing it on a compatible platform, such as Moodle.

Custom texts

This tab lets us customise the text and automatic messages generated by the iDevice.

odeComponent.htmlView:
We'll use this iDevice to create games in which players have to classify cards with images, text and/or sounds in different categories previously created.

Depending on the difficulty level, we can create games with different options:

  • Level basic: A card can be placed in any category. Green or red borders indicate whether it is correct or incorrect, and a customisable correct or incorrect message is displayed. Cards can be moved
  • Level intermediate: A card can be placed in any category and moved. Clicking Check displays the results and score.
  • Level advanced: Once a card has been placed in a category, it cannot be moved. Green or red borders indicate whether it is correct or incorrect, and a customisable correct or incorrect message is displayed.

Selecting “Classify” from the iDevices list displays the following in eXeLearning:

At the top, we can change the title and assign an icon. Several options and tabs have different functions, allowing us to configure the game flexibly

General settings


The “General settings” tab is displayed by default when you create the Classify iDevice.

In this tab, we define the game instructions, available options and settings, and questions with the clues we choose.

  • Clicking “Instructions” opens a text box where we can enter the instructions to follow.
  • Clicking the “Options” section lets us choose the game difficulty (basic, intermediate or advanced), whether to add “Custom messages”, define the names of up to four categories for classification, choose whether the game starts minimised, set the game time, define a feedback message and the percentage of questions required to pass, and set authorship. The Progress report is configured in “Grading”.
  • Under the Section "Cards," for each of them we will be able to introduce:
    • The text / image / audio for the first card, with its corresponding group.
    • The text / image / audio for the second card, with its corresponding group.
    • The same for the third, fourth, etc...

Passwords

In the “Passwords” tab, we can create a sequence of challenges in which players cannot access a new game until they obtain a key from a previous activity. We can set an access code and a message shown to players when they reach a specified percentage of correct answers, which they can use as the password for a new challenge or subsequent activity. 

Both are optional, and their settings only appear when we enable them, as shown in the image.

Grading

  • SCORM: lets us save the score automatically or using a button, or choose not to save it. The available options depend on the iDevice.
  • Progress report: includes the activity in the report and shows its identifier.
  • Minimum score to pass the activity: uses the project’s global value or lets you select “Custom”.

Saving scores through SCORM requires exporting the content as SCORM and publishing it on a compatible platform, such as Moodle.

Custom texts

This tab lets us customise the text and automatic messages generated by the iDevice.

Import / Export

On the "Import / Export" tab we can import questions compatible with this activity from TXT or XML (Moodle) files, or we can export questions in txt format to integrate them into other compatible activities.

AI

This tab makes it easy to import questions from an AI chatbot. It shows an example prompt that we can take to a chatbot to generate questions in the correct format for pasting into the “Questions” tab. When we save, the AI-generated questions are added to the iDevice, ready to use in the activity.

We'll use this iDevice to create activities in which students fill gaps in a text by typing, selecting or dragging the answers.

This iDevice’s flexibility allows us to create up to four different types of activity:

  • Complete (writing word or string of words)
  • Drag (dragging each word into its corresponding gap)
  • Select (choosing a word from a dropdown containing all the hidden words)
  • Select (by limiting words from each drop-down box)

The cell (from the Latin cellula, a diminutive of cella, ‘cell’) is the @@morphological|mitochondrion|chloroplast|vacuole|ribosome@@ and functional unit of every @@living organism|mitochondrion|chloroplast|vacuole|ribosome@@. In fact, the cell is the smallest element that can be considered alive. ​ Living organisms can therefore be classified according to the number of cells they have: if they have only one, they are called @@unicellular@@ (such as protozoa or bacteria, which are microscopic organisms); if they have more, they are called @@multicellular@@ .

The cell (from the Latin cellula, a diminutive of cella, ‘cell’) is the @@morphological|mitochondrion|chloroplast|vacuole|ribosome@@ and functional unit of every @@living organism|mitochondrion|chloroplast|vacuole|ribosome@@. In fact, the cell is the smallest element that can be considered alive. ​ Living organisms can therefore be classified according to the number of cells they have: if they have only one, they are called @@unicellular@@ (such as protozoa or bacteria, which are microscopic organisms); if they have more, they are called @@multicellular@@ .

Selecting “Fill in the gaps” from the iDevices list displays the following in eXeLearning:

At the top, we can change the title and assign an icon. Several options and tabs have different functions, allowing us to configure the game flexibly

General settings


The “General settings” tab is displayed by default when you create the Fill in the gaps iDevice.

In this tab, we define the instructions for playing the game, the various available options and settings, and the texts with gaps.

  • Clicking “Instructions” opens a text box where we can enter the instructions to follow.
  • Clicking the “Options” section lets us choose the game type (Fill in, Drag, Select, and Select with a limited set of words in each dropdown), the number of attempts, the time, whether to show solutions or allow errors, whether answers are case-sensitive, whether gap sizes are proportional to the hidden words, whether the game is minimised, and whether to give feedback when a percentage of correct answers is reached at the end of the game. 
  • In the Text section, after entering the text with images, videos or any other resource provided by the eXeLearning editor, we hide the words or text strings we choose by placing a double @ at the beginning and end of each word or string to hide

Passwords

In the “Passwords” tab, we can create a sequence of challenges in which players cannot access a new game until they obtain a key from a previous activity. We can set an access code and a message shown to players when they reach a specified percentage of correct answers, which they can use as the password for a new challenge or subsequent activity. 

Both are optional, and their settings only appear when we enable them, as shown in the image.

Grading

  • SCORM: lets us save the score automatically or using a button, or choose not to save it. The available options depend on the iDevice.
  • Progress report: includes the activity in the report and shows its identifier.
  • Minimum score to pass the activity: uses the project’s global value or lets you select “Custom”.

Saving scores through SCORM requires exporting the content as SCORM and publishing it on a compatible platform, such as Moodle.

Custom texts

This tab lets us customise the text and automatic messages generated by the iDevice.

Selecting “Scrambled list” from the iDevices list displays the following in eXeLearning:

At the top, we can change the title and assign an icon. Several options and tabs have different functions, allowing us to configure the game flexibly

General settings

The “General settings” tab is displayed by default when you create the Scrambled list iDevice.

In this tab, we define the activities in the iDevice, instructions for completing them, settings and options, and the definitions of the words or expressions our students should know.

  • Clicking “Instructions” opens a text box where we can enter the instructions to follow.
  • In the “List” tab, we add the items in the correct order. The program will display them in a scrambled order for the student to arrange correctly. We can add instructions at the beginning and change the button text and feedback. The “Grading” tab lets us include the result in the Progress report iDevice.

Custom texts

This tab lets us customise the text and automatic messages generated by the iDevice.

Grading

  • SCORM: lets us save the score automatically or using a button, or choose not to save it. The available options depend on the iDevice.
  • Progress report: includes the activity in the report and shows its identifier.
  • Minimum score to pass the activity: uses the project’s global value or lets you select “Custom”.

Saving scores through SCORM requires exporting the content as SCORM and publishing it on a compatible platform, such as Moodle.

Import / Export

On the "Import / Export" tab we can import questions compatible with this activity from TXT or XML (Moodle) files, or we can export questions in txt format to integrate them into other compatible activities.

AI

This tab makes it easy to import questions from an AI chatbot. It shows an example prompt that we can take to a chatbot to generate questions in the correct format for pasting into the “Questions” tab. When we save, the AI-generated questions are added to the iDevice, ready to use in the activity.

At the top, we can change the title and assign an icon. Several options and tabs have different functions, allowing us to configure the game flexibly

General settings


The “General settings” tab is displayed by default when you create the Identify iDevice.

In this tab, we define the game instructions, available options and settings, and questions with the clues we choose.

  • Clicking “Instructions” opens a text box where we can enter the instructions to follow.
  • Clicking the “Options” section lets us choose whether the game is minimised, enable advanced mode to deduct points each time a student reveals a clue (when advanced mode is disabled, students can access all clues without affecting their final score), shuffle questions, show custom messages, solutions and the time, provide specific feedback at the end of the game if a certain percentage of correct answers is reached, and set the number of questions to display. The Progress report is configured in “Grading”.
  • Under the Section "Questions," for each of them we can introduce:
    • The question prompt or message.
    • The solution.
    • A related image.
    • The number of attempts allowed to answer the question.
    • The number of clues accompanying each question.

Passwords

In the “Passwords” tab, we can create a sequence of challenges in which players cannot access a new game until they obtain a key from a previous activity. We can set an access code and a message shown to players when they reach a specified percentage of correct answers, which they can use as the password for a new challenge or subsequent activity. 

Both are optional, and their settings only appear when we enable them, as shown in the image.

Grading

  • SCORM: lets us save the score automatically or using a button, or choose not to save it. The available options depend on the iDevice.
  • Progress report: includes the activity in the report and shows its identifier.
  • Minimum score to pass the activity: uses the project’s global value or lets you select “Custom”.

Saving scores through SCORM requires exporting the content as SCORM and publishing it on a compatible platform, such as Moodle.

Custom texts

This tab lets us customise the text and automatic messages generated by the iDevice.

Import / Export

On the "Import / Export" tab we can import questions compatible with this activity from TXT or XML (Moodle) files, or we can export questions in txt format to integrate them into other compatible activities.

AI

This tab makes it easy to import questions from an AI chatbot. It shows an example prompt that we can take to a chatbot to generate questions in the correct format for pasting into the “Questions” tab. When we save, the AI-generated questions are added to the iDevice, ready to use in the activity.

Selecting “Order” from the iDevices list displays the following in eXeLearning:

At the top, we can change the title and assign an icon. Several options and tabs have different functions, allowing us to configure the game flexibly

General settings


The “General settings” tab is displayed by default when you create the Order iDevice.

In this tab, we define the instructions for playing the game and the various available options and settings.

  • Clicking “Instructions” opens a text box where we can enter the instructions to follow.
  • Clicking the “Options” section lets us choose whether to order “sentences” or “multimedia”
Options (SENTENCES)
  • In the option "Sentences”, we decide whether the game starts minimised, the game time, whether to show solutions, the feedback message, the percentage of questions required to pass the game, and authorship. The Progress report is configured in “Grading”.
  • In the “Activities” section, under “Sentences”, we can enter the sentence to be ordered
Options (MULTIMEDIA)
  • In the option "Multimedia” we decide whether the game starts minimised, whether cards remain visible for a set time, whether to customise correct and incorrect answer messages, and the game time. We can also choose whether to show solutions, define a feedback message, the percentage of questions required to pass the game, authorship, and the number of columns for ordering, with the option of fixed headers or automatic start. The Progress report is configured in “Grading”.
  • In the “Activities” section, under “Multimedia”, we can define the task in the prompt using text or audio and add as many texts, images or audio clips as we want to order.

Passwords

In the “Passwords” tab, we can create a sequence of challenges in which players cannot access a new game until they obtain a key from a previous activity. We can set an access code and a message shown to players when they reach a specified percentage of correct answers, which they can use as the password for a new challenge or subsequent activity. 

Both are optional, and their settings only appear when we enable them, as shown in the image.

Grading

  • SCORM: lets us save the score automatically or using a button, or choose not to save it. The available options depend on the iDevice.
  • Progress report: includes the activity in the report and shows its identifier.
  • Minimum score to pass the activity: uses the project’s global value or lets you select “Custom”.

Saving scores through SCORM requires exporting the content as SCORM and publishing it on a compatible platform, such as Moodle.

Custom texts

This tab lets us customise the text and automatic messages generated by the iDevice.

Import / Export

On the "Import / Export" tab we can import questions compatible with this activity from TXT or XML (Moodle) files, or we can export questions in txt format to integrate them into other compatible activities.

  • In the option "Sentences”, we decide whether the game starts minimised, the game time, whether to show solutions, the feedback message, the percentage of questions required to pass the game, and authorship. The Progress report is configured in “Grading”.
  • In the “Activities” section, under “Sentences”, we can enter the sentence to be ordered
Options (MULTIMEDIA)
  • In the option "Multimedia” we decide whether the game starts minimised, whether cards remain visible for a set time, whether to customise correct and incorrect answer messages, and the game time. We can also choose whether to show solutions, define a feedback message, the percentage of questions required to pass the game, authorship, and the number of columns for ordering, with the option of fixed headers or automatic start. The Progress report is configured in “Grading”.
  • In the “Activities” section, under “Multimedia”, we can define the task in the prompt using text or audio and add as many texts, images or audio clips as we want to order.

Passwords

In the “Passwords” tab, we can create a sequence of challenges in which players cannot access a new game until they obtain a key from a previous activity. We can set an access code and a message shown to players when they reach a specified percentage of correct answers, which they can use as the password for a new challenge or subsequent activity. 

Both are optional, and their settings only appear when we enable them, as shown in the image.

Grading

  • SCORM: lets us save the score automatically or using a button, or choose not to save it. The available options depend on the iDevice.
  • Progress report: includes the activity in the report and shows its identifier.
  • Minimum score to pass the activity: uses the project’s global value or lets you select “Custom”.

Saving scores through SCORM requires exporting the content as SCORM and publishing it on a compatible platform, such as Moodle.

Custom texts

This tab lets us customise the text and automatic messages generated by the iDevice.

Import / Export

On the "Import / Export" tab we can import questions compatible with this activity from TXT or XML (Moodle) files, or we can export questions in txt format to integrate them into other compatible activities.

We use this iDevice to create games in which concepts are matched by connecting them with arrows. Images, sounds and rich text can be used.

Depending on the difficulty level, we can create games with different options:

  • Basic level: Cards can only be connected to their matching card (the score will always be 10 once all pairs have been connected).
  • Intermediate level: Cards are connected to each other, then clicking Check displays the results and score.
  • Advanced level: The same as the intermediate level, but with a configurable time limit.

Selecting “Relate” from the iDevices list displays the following in eXeLearning:

At the top, we can change the title and assign an icon. Several options and tabs have different functions, allowing us to configure the game flexibly

General settings


The “General settings” tab is displayed by default when you create the Relate iDevice.

In this tab, we define the game instructions, available options and settings, and questions with the clues we choose.

  • Clicking “Instructions” opens a text box where we can enter the instructions to follow.
  • Clicking the “Options” section lets us choose the game difficulty (basic, intermediate or advanced), whether the game is minimised, the percentage of all entered pairs to show in each round, and the game’s authorship. To include the result in the “Progress report” iDevice, use the “Grading” tab.
  • In the “Pairs” section, we can enter the following for each pair:
    • The text / image / audio for the first card in the pair.
    • The text / image / audio for the second card in the pair.
    • There is also an option to reverse the cards.

Passwords

In the “Passwords” tab, we can create a sequence of challenges in which players cannot access a new game until they obtain a key from a previous activity. We can set an access code and a message shown to players when they reach a specified percentage of correct answers, which they can use as the password for a new challenge or subsequent activity. 

Both are optional, and their settings only appear when we enable them, as shown in the image.

Grading

  • SCORM: lets us save the score automatically or using a button, or choose not to save it. The available options depend on the iDevice.
  • Progress report: includes the activity in the report and shows its identifier.
  • Minimum score to pass the activity: uses the project’s global value or lets you select “Custom”.

Saving scores through SCORM requires exporting the content as SCORM and publishing it on a compatible platform, such as Moodle.

Custom texts

This tab lets us customise the text and automatic messages generated by the iDevice.

Import / Export

On the "Import / Export" tab we can import questions compatible with this activity from TXT or XML (Moodle) files, or we can export questions in txt format to integrate them into other compatible activities.

AI

This tab makes it easy to import questions from an AI chatbot. It shows an example prompt that we can take to a chatbot to generate questions in the correct format for pasting into the “Questions” tab. When we save, the AI-generated questions are added to the iDevice, ready to use in the activity.
