Selecting “Memory cards” from the iDevices list displays the following in eXeLearning:

At the top, we can change the title and assign an icon. Several options and tabs have different functions, allowing us to configure the game flexibly

General settings

The “General settings” tab is displayed by default when you create the Memory cards iDevice.

In this tab, we define the instructions for playing the game, the various available options and settings, and the cards to display.

  • Clicking “Instructions” opens a text box where we can enter the instructions to follow.
  • By clicking on the "Options" Section we can decide:
    • The game type we want to use (show, navigation, identify and memory)
    • The “Memory” type lets you adjust the game time.
    • The option to display the cards randomly.
    • Percentage of cards to be shown in the game.
    • In “Grading”, enable the Progress report and enter its identifier.
  • Under "Cards," we can:
    • Enter the front and back (the front is shown by default and the back is revealed by the student)
    • Use text, images and audio on each side

We can always reverse one card or all cards by clicking the corresponding links (Reverse card, Reverse all cards)

Passwords

In the “Passwords” tab, we can create a sequence of challenges in which players cannot access a new game until they obtain a key from a previous activity. We can set an access code and a message shown to players when they reach a specified percentage of correct answers, which they can use as the password for a new challenge or subsequent activity. 

Both are optional, and their settings only appear when we enable them, as shown in the image.

Grading

  • SCORM: lets us save the score automatically or using a button, or choose not to save it. The available options depend on the iDevice.
  • Progress report: includes the activity in the report and shows its identifier.
  • Minimum score to pass the activity: uses the project’s global value or lets you select “Custom”.

Saving scores through SCORM requires exporting the content as SCORM and publishing it on a compatible platform, such as Moodle.

Custom texts

This tab lets us customise the text and automatic messages generated by the iDevice.

Import / Export

On the "Import / Export" tab we can import questions compatible with this activity from TXT or XML (Moodle) files, or we can export questions in txt format to integrate them into other compatible activities.

AI

This tab makes it easy to import questions from an AI chatbot. It shows an example prompt that we can take to a chatbot to generate questions in the correct format for pasting into the “Questions” tab. When we save, the AI-generated questions are added to the iDevice, ready to use in the activity.

odeComponent.htmlView:
These resources are designed specifically to work with contents of specific subjects or areas, making it easier to integrate specialised tools for teaching scientific subjects. eXeLearning allows a wide variety of materials and interactive activities to be included to enrich content; these iDevices extend this capability to specialised fields, in this case science.

Within this category, available iDevices include:

  • 3Dmol
  • Electrical circuits
  • GeoGebra
  • Math operations
  • Math problems
  • Periodic Table

odeComponent.htmlView: Lets you create interactive quizzes based on 3D molecular models that can be viewed directly in the content. Users can load models in compatible formats, choose display styles and configure questions with options, timing and order. It is useful for educational chemistry and biology activities, combining visual exploration and interactive assessment.

Selecting “3Dmol” from the iDevices list displays the following in eXeLearning:

At the top, we can change the title and assign an icon. There are several options and tabs, each with a different function, allowing us to configure our activity very flexibly

General settings


The “General settings” tab is displayed by default when you create the iDevice.

In this tab, we define the instructions, the various available options and settings, and the questions with our chosen clues.

  • Clicking the “Instructions” opens a text box where we can enter the instructions to follow.
  • Clicking the “Options"we can decide:
Test option

This is shown in the image above and consists of creating a quiz using the various options shown.

    "Presentation" option

    Instead of a quiz, the content is displayed as a presentation.

    • The “Questions” section is where we add, in the appropriate format, the 3D file, and we define the question or display options depending on whether we have chosen “Test” or “Presentation”. We can also choose the style in which the molecule is displayed.

    Passwords

    In the “Passwords” tab, we can create a sequence of challenges in which players cannot access a new game until they obtain a key from a previous activity. We can set an access code and a message shown to players when they reach a specified percentage of correct answers, which they can use as the password for a new challenge or subsequent activity. 

    Both are optional, and their settings only appear when we enable them, as shown in the image.

    Grading

    • SCORM: lets us save the score automatically or using a button, or choose not to save it. The available options depend on the iDevice.
    • Progress report: includes the activity in the report and shows its identifier.
    • Minimum score to pass the activity: uses the project’s global value or lets you select “Custom”.

    Saving scores through SCORM requires exporting the content as SCORM and publishing it on a compatible platform, such as Moodle.

    Custom texts

    This tab lets us customise the text and automatic messages generated by the iDevice.

    • PDB (.pdb): most widely used format for proteins and other biomolecules.
    • SDF (.sdf): suitable for small molecules; can store multiple molecules and metadata.
    • MOL2 (.mol2): includes atom types, charges and bonds; widely used in molecular docking.
    • XYZ (.xyz): a simple format with only atomic coordinates.
    • CIF / mmCIF (.cif, .mmcif): standard for crystalline and macromolecular structures.
    • ZIP / TGZ / GZ: compression formats to distribute file sets.

Selecting “Electrical circuits” from the iDevices list displays the following in eXeLearning:

At the top, we can change the title and assign an icon. There are several options and tabs, each with a different function, allowing us to configure our activity very flexibly

General settings


The “General settings” tab is displayed by default when you create the iDevice.

In this tab, we define the instructions, the various available options and settings, and the questions with our chosen clues.

  • Clicking the “Instructions” opens a text box where we can enter the instructions to follow.
  • Clicking the “Options"we can decide:
Test option

This is shown in the image above and consists of creating a quiz using the various options shown.

    "Presentation" option

    Instead of a quiz, the content is displayed as a presentation.

    • The “Questions” section is where we add the code to display the circuit and we define the question or display options depending on whether we have chosen “Test” or “Presentation”. Options include the number of choices, timing, etc.

    Passwords

    In the “Passwords” tab, we can create a sequence of challenges in which players cannot access a new game until they obtain a key from a previous activity. We can set an access code and a message shown to players when they reach a specified percentage of correct answers, which they can use as the password for a new challenge or subsequent activity. 

    Both are optional, and their settings only appear when we enable them, as shown in the image.

    Grading

    • SCORM: lets us save the score automatically or using a button, or choose not to save it. The available options depend on the iDevice.
    • Progress report: includes the activity in the report and shows its identifier.
    • Minimum score to pass the activity: uses the project’s global value or lets you select “Custom”.

    Saving scores through SCORM requires exporting the content as SCORM and publishing it on a compatible platform, such as Moodle.

    Custom texts

    This tab lets us customise the text and automatic messages generated by the iDevice.

    AI

    This tab makes it easy to import questions from an AI chatbot. It shows an example prompt that we can take to a chatbot to generate questions in the correct format for pasting into the “Questions” tab. When we save, the AI-generated questions are added to the iDevice, ready to use in the activity.

Selecting “GeoGebra” from the iDevices list displays the following in eXeLearning:

At the top, we can change the title and assign an icon. There are several options, each with a different function, allowing us to configure our game very flexibly

General settings

  • In the “Instructions” section, we write the instructions for the activity.
  • In “General settings”, we enter the URL of the activity created with GeoGebra and can set its displayed width and height.
  • The “Advanced options” section contains more display options. Saving the score and including it in the Progress report are configured in the “Grading” tab.

Cedec. GeoGebra advanced options (CC BY-SA)

Grading

  • SCORM: lets us save the score automatically or using a button, or choose not to save it. The available options depend on the iDevice.
  • Progress report: includes the activity in the report and shows its identifier.
  • Minimum score to pass the activity: uses the project’s global value or lets you select “Custom”.

Saving scores through SCORM requires exporting the content as SCORM and publishing it on a compatible platform, such as Moodle.

We'll use this iDevice to create activities with basic mathematical operations (addition, subtraction, multiplication and/or division) at random, in which students have to work out the result, operator or one of the operands.

Due to the flexibility of this iDevice, we can define:

  • Whether we want students to work out the result, operator, first or second operand, or any of the above.
  • The highest and lowest numbers, the number of operations and the decimal places
  • Errors (relative and / or absolute)

Selecting “Math operations” from the iDevices list displays the following in eXeLearning:

At the top, we can change the title and assign an icon. Several options and tabs have different functions, allowing us to configure the game flexibly

General settings


The “General settings” tab is displayed by default when you create the Math operations iDevice.

In this tab, we define the game instructions, available options and settings, and questions with the clues we choose.

  • Clicking “Instructions” opens a text box where we can enter the instructions to follow.
  • By clicking on the "Options" Section we can decide:
With the “Fractions” checkbox disabled (Elementary operations)

The element to work out: result, operator, operands or random; the number of operations and number range; the number of decimal places in the operands; the operation type (addition, subtraction, multiplication or division); and options such as allowing decimal results, negative numbers, zero and errors. We can also set a time limit for the activity.
The Progress report is configured in “Grading”.

    With the “Fractions” checkbox enabled (Fraction operations)

    The element to work out: result, operator, operands or random; the number of operations and number range; the number of decimal places in the operands; the operation type (addition, subtraction, multiplication or division); and options such as allowing negative numbers or fractions in their simplest form. We can set a time limit for the activity. The Progress report is configured in “Grading”.

    Passwords

    In the “Passwords” tab, we can create a sequence of challenges in which players cannot access a new game until they obtain a key from a previous activity. We can set an access code and a message shown to players when they reach a specified percentage of correct answers, which they can use as the password for a new challenge or subsequent activity. 

    Both are optional, and their settings only appear when we enable them, as shown in the image.

    Grading

    • SCORM: lets us save the score automatically or using a button, or choose not to save it. The available options depend on the iDevice.
    • Progress report: includes the activity in the report and shows its identifier.
    • Minimum score to pass the activity: uses the project’s global value or lets you select “Custom”.

    Saving scores through SCORM requires exporting the content as SCORM and publishing it on a compatible platform, such as Moodle.

    Custom texts

    This tab lets us customise the text and automatic messages generated by the iDevice.

Selecting “Math problems” from the iDevices list displays the following in eXeLearning:

At the top, we can change the title and assign an icon. Several options and tabs have different functions, allowing us to configure the game flexibly

General settings


The “General settings” tab is displayed by default when you create the Math problems iDevice.

In this tab, we define the game instructions, available options and settings, and questions with the clues we choose.

  • Clicking “Instructions” opens a text box where we can enter the instructions to follow.
  • By clicking on the "Options" Section we can decide:
    • Show minimized, solutions and questions at random.
    • Allowed errors.
    • Percentage of questions to be shown in the game.
    • In “Grading”, enable the Progress report and enter its identifier.
  • In the problems section, we can enter the different problems to include in the game, bearing in mind that we can configure:
    • The time to solve every problem
    • The mathematical expression that solves the problem (written in JSMath; see the help links)
    • The problem statement, where variables must be written so that random numbers are displayed in JSMath.
    • Define the range of numbers available when generating questions and whether to use decimals
    • Define the domain of each variable 
    • Choose the lowest and highest numbers, or the number of decimal places

Passwords

In the “Passwords” tab, we can create a sequence of challenges in which players cannot access a new game until they obtain a key from a previous activity. We can set an access code and a message shown to players when they reach a specified percentage of correct answers, which they can use as the password for a new challenge or subsequent activity. 

Both are optional, and their settings only appear when we enable them, as shown in the image.

Grading

  • SCORM: lets us save the score automatically or using a button, or choose not to save it. The available options depend on the iDevice.
  • Progress report: includes the activity in the report and shows its identifier.
  • Minimum score to pass the activity: uses the project’s global value or lets you select “Custom”.

Saving scores through SCORM requires exporting the content as SCORM and publishing it on a compatible platform, such as Moodle.

Custom texts

This tab lets us customise the text and automatic messages generated by the iDevice.

Selecting “Periodic table” from the iDevices list displays the following in eXeLearning:

At the top, we can change the title and assign an icon. Several options and tabs have different functions, allowing us to configure the game flexibly

General settings


The “General settings” tab is displayed by default when you create the Periodic table iDevice

In this tab, we define the activities in the iDevice, instructions for completing them, settings and options, and the definitions of the words or expressions our students should know.

  • Clicking “Instructions” opens a text box where we can enter the instructions to follow.
  • Clicking the “Options” section lets us configure the mode (Game, Complete and Mobile), choose names, symbols and groups, set the number of questions and attempts, and show solutions. The Progress report is configured in “Grading”.

    Passwords

    In the “Passwords” tab, we can create a sequence of challenges in which players cannot access a new game until they obtain a key from a previous activity. We can set an access code and a message shown to players when they reach a specified percentage of correct answers, which they can use as the password for a new challenge or subsequent activity. 

    Both are optional, and their settings only appear when we enable them, as shown in the image.

    Grading

    • SCORM: lets us save the score automatically or using a button, or choose not to save it. The available options depend on the iDevice.
    • Progress report: includes the activity in the report and shows its identifier.
    • Minimum score to pass the activity: uses the project’s global value or lets you select “Custom”.

    Saving scores through SCORM requires exporting the content as SCORM and publishing it on a compatible platform, such as Moodle.

    Custom texts

    This tab lets us customise the text and automatic messages generated by the iDevice.

odeComponent.htmlView:
Once we have finished our material in eXeLearning, the most satisfying moment remains: sharing our project with others. We can publish and share it in different ways depending on how we want to use it.

The resource we have created will be preserved with an extension .elpx, an extension that is only valid for editing the project with this version of the tool. To allow other users to view the generated content and upload it to different repositories, platforms or LMSs, eXeLearning lets us download or export projects in different formats. 

NOTE. If we work with the Cloud version of eXeLearning integrated into a platform or LMS, publishing to that platform is as simple as clicking a button.

odeComponent.htmlView:
eXeLearning makes it easy to download the materials we create in different formats, allowing them to be used in different ways and contexts. There are some differences between the desktop and online versions and the Cloud version, as we will see below.

Desktop / online version

In this case, we have access to our computer to save the elpx file. We can export the content in various formats:


Available export formats:

  • Website: generates a compressed file (.zip) containing the material organised into web pages. To view it, extract the archive and double-click the file index.html, at the root of the package.
  • Export into folder (Uncompressed Website): exports the project’s files and folders to the folder you specify on your computer.
  • Single page: downloads a compressed file (.zip) containing all the content on a single web page. As with the previous format, extract it and open the file index.html.
  • SCORM 1.2: an educational standard widely used to publish content on LMS platforms. It includes the project’s content and metadata and allows students’ progress and grades to be tracked. To view it, it must be uploaded to an LMS that supports SCORM, such as Moodle. This is the recommended version for these platforms.
  • IMS Content Package (IMS CP): a standard compatible with LMS platforms that includes content and metadata. Unlike SCORM, it does not allow progress tracking or the collection of grades.
  • ePub3: an open format for electronic books. Unlike PDF, ePub files do not have a fixed page size, as the content adapts to the device’s screen size. It appears on more pages on small screens and fewer pages on large screens.

Cloud Version

In this case, we have several options for downloading our material to our computer:

Available download formats:

  • Content of eXeLearning (.elpx): lets us download the project as an .elpx file, directly editable in eXeLearning. 
  • Website: generates a compressed file (.zip) containing the material organised into web pages. To view it, extract the archive and double-click the file index.html, at the root of the package.
  • Single page: downloads a compressed file (.zip) containing all the content on a single web page. As with the previous format, extract it and open the file index.html.
  • SCORM 1.2: an educational standard widely used to publish content on LMS platforms. It includes the project’s content and metadata and allows students’ progress and grades to be tracked. To view it, it must be uploaded to an LMS that supports SCORM, such as Moodle. This is the recommended version for these platforms.
  • IMS Content Package (IMS CP): a standard compatible with LMS platforms that includes content and metadata. Unlike SCORM, it does not allow progress tracking or the collection of grades.
  • ePub3: an open format for electronic books. Unlike PDF, ePub files do not have a fixed page size, as the content adapts to the device’s screen size. It appears on more pages on small screens and fewer pages on large screens.

odeComponent.htmlView:
Print the resource or prepare an activity worksheet

In File → Print opens a full-screen preview with the Print options on the right. Options are reflected in the preview without closing it. New labels may appear in English while translations are being completed.

The print options have 3 sections:

Document

  • Show link URLs: adds the address in square brackets after the link text; enabled by default.
  • Print the contents of minimized boxes: expands collapsed boxes. If you do not enable it, what you see is printed: you can collapse or expand boxes in the preview. Hidden content remains excluded.
  • Print teacher-only content: Only appears when teacher mode is enabled in a box or iDevice

What do you want to print?

When the project contains interactive activities, choose how to put them on paper:

Option Outcome
Content with activities Replaces each activity with its exercise in the same position in the document.
Content with activities in an appendix The default option. Leaves a reference in the document and groups the numbered exercises at the end; each starts on a new page.
Activities only (without other content) Creates a worksheet with the project title and name and date fields. Each exercise starts on a new page.
Content without activities prints the document without activities.

Activities

Select the activities you want to include, or select all. 

Not all activities have a paper equivalent. TriviExt, Map, GeoGebra, Progress report, Puzzle, Interactive video, Video test, External website, Download source file, File attachments and Magnifier are not printed as exercises. The option Show titles of non-printable activities lets you include their titles and a notice that they are unavailable in print. Video questions and other multimedia elements that cannot be transferred to paper are omitted; check the note for teachers in the preview about excluded elements.

Styles adapt to white paper: backgrounds are not printed. Check page breaks and readability before printing.

Press Print to send the preview to the print dialogue. In the browser, choose Save as PDF there if available. In the desktop application, the button Save as PDF saves the preview directly without requiring an installed printer; the suggested filename is the project title.

If printing does not start, the preview displays a notice: in the browser, it offers to open the document in another tab; on the desktop, it allows you to save it as a PDF. You can close the preview with Close or Esc.

odeComponent.htmlView:
Having reviewed the export and offline-use options, we can go a step further and see how to publish and share our materials with others. The available options are:

  • Share with eXeViewer
  • Export and upload to an educational resource platform such as Procomún
  • Export and upload to Moodle

eXeLearning currently offers various plugins and integrations to create, edit and publish content on different platforms such as Moodle, WordPress, Omeka-S, NextCloud, OneDrive and Google Drive. If you use eXeLearning plugins and integrations, you will find that editing is similar to what is explained throughout this manual. However, publishing may vary depending on the chosen integration, so we recommend consulting the manual “eXeLearning integration solutions".

odePagStructure.blockName: eXeViewer, the solution to share your materials

odeComponent.htmlView:
eXeViewer is a free, open-source web application that lets us open and view resources created with eXeLearning directly in the browser, without installing software or creating user accounts. It is designed to make materials easier to share when we do not have Moodle, WordPress, a blog or a server on which to publish the resource.

With eXeViewer, we can open two types of files: the .elpx file used by eXeLearning, or a .zip file generated by exporting the project as a website. One of its main advantages is that processing takes place in the browser itself, so files are not uploaded to an external server.

The tool offers two forms of use:

  • Load a file directly. We can drag an .elpx or .zip file from our computer and open it in the browser. This is useful for projecting the resource in class, reviewing it or using it locally. Once loaded, it can work even where connectivity is limited.
  • Load from a URL. We can enter the address of an .elpx or .zip file stored in the cloud or on a server. eXeViewer generates a link we can share with students so they can open the resource directly in their browser.

This option is especially useful when we want to share an OER quickly while retaining its navigation and interactivity, without students needing to install anything. We can host the file on services such as Nextcloud, Google Drive, OneDrive or an institutional server, provided the link allows the file to be downloaded directly.

We also have the option of installing it on our computer and using it offline.

NOTE. eXeViewer does not record students’ progress, generate grades or store files. The shared link will work as long as the file remains available at its original location. Some cloud services may also have size limits or download restrictions.

In summary, eXeViewer is a simple solution for viewing, reviewing and sharing eXeLearning resources with students without technical barriers. We only need the resource file and, if we want to share it online, a stable link to the file.

odeComponent.htmlView:
Procomún is an open educational resources network run by the Ministry of Education, Vocational Training and Sports, where teachers can find, use, share and publish educational materials. It provides access to openly licensed resources organised by educational stage, subject area and competencies, and makes it easier for other teachers to reuse, adapt and improve them.

Materials created with eXeLearning and exported in SCORM format can currently be published, with a difference between versions:

  • Materials created with eXeLearning 2.9 and earlier: can be published as SCORM and edited with eXeLearning online.
  • Materials created with eXeLearning 3.0 and later: can be published as SCORM but cannot yet be edited. This feature will be available soon.

The steps to be taken would be: 

  • Export our resource to SCORM
  • Once logged into Procomún, upload the SCORM file as a new Learning resource.
  • Complete the fields in the form displayed
  • Publish.

If the resource can be edited with eXe online, an edit button like the one below will appear once it is published.

odeComponent.htmlView:
We can upload content created with eXeLearning to a Moodle platform in different formats, such as Website, SCORM or IMS Content Package. If the Moodle platform has the eXeScorm and/or eXeWeb plugins installed, content can also be created and edited directly within the LMS, without leaving the platform.

In either case, we must be clear about the format in which we want to present the materials in Moodle: SCORM, IMS or Website.

  • SCORM: If we want to save grades from iDevices that offer this option and track the pages viewed by students. For now, export is only available in SCORM 1.2 because Moodle does not currently support SCORM 2004.
  • IMS: If we only want to display the content but want the package to retain its metadata when uploaded to Moodle.
  • Website: If we only want to display the content and do not need metadata. This is the most advisable option if we have not used the iDevices mentioned above, as it provides a more attractive display, as shown below.

Steps:

Publication as SCORM

STEPS:

  1. Add a “SCORM package” activity.
  2. Enter the details and upload our SCORM package.
  3. Save.
  4. To view it, click the activity title and then the Enter button. Moodle uses its own SCORM viewer to display the resource, so its appearance may differ from how it originally looked in eXeLearning.

Publish as IMS

STEPS:

  1. Add an “IMS content package” resource.
  2. Enter the details and upload our IMS file.
  3. Save.
  4. To view it, click the resource title. Moodle uses its own IMS viewer to display the resource, so its appearance may differ from how it originally looked in eXeLearning.

Publication as a Website

STEPS:

  1. Add a “File” resource.
  2. Enter the details and upload our Website file (.zip). 
  3. Click the uploaded file. In the window that appears, click Unzip. A series of files and folders will appear.
  4. We click on the file index.html and, in the window that appears, click Set main file.
  5. Save
  6. To view it, click the resource title. In this case, all the content is displayed with the menu and style defined in eXeLearning.

We can upload content created with eXeLearning to a Moodle platform in different formats, such as Website, SCORM or IMS Content Package. If the Moodle platform has the eXeScorm and/or eXeWeb plugins installed, content can also be created and edited directly within the LMS, without leaving the platform.

In either case, we must be clear about the format in which we want to present the materials in Moodle: SCORM, IMS or Website.

  • SCORM: If we want to save grades from iDevices that offer this option and track the pages viewed by students. For now, export is only available in SCORM 1.2 because Moodle does not currently support SCORM 2004.
  • IMS: If we only want to display the content but want the package to retain its metadata when uploaded to Moodle.
  • Website: If we only want to display the content and do not need metadata. This is the most advisable option if we have not used the iDevices mentioned above, as it provides a more attractive display, as shown below.

Steps:

Publication as SCORM

STEPS:

  1. Add a “SCORM package” activity.
  2. Enter the details and upload our SCORM package.
  3. Save.
  4. To view it, click the activity title and then the Enter button. Moodle uses its own SCORM viewer to display the resource, so its appearance may differ from how it originally looked in eXeLearning.

Publish as IMS

STEPS:

  1. Add an “IMS content package” resource.
  2. Enter the details and upload our IMS file.
  3. Save.
  4. To view it, click the resource title. Moodle uses its own IMS viewer to display the resource, so its appearance may differ from how it originally looked in eXeLearning.

Publication as a Website

STEPS:

  1. Add a “File” resource.
  2. Enter the details and upload our Website file (.zip). 
  3. Click the uploaded file. In the window that appears, click Unzip. A series of files and folders will appear.
  4. We click on the file index.html and, in the window that appears, click Set main file.
  5. Save
  6. To view it, click the resource title. In this case, all the content is displayed with the menu and style defined in eXeLearning.
